tasks.title: Phase 5A: Codebase inventory and DesigoLogWatcher project scaffold
tasks.description: Inventory Watch 0.4.0 as the behavioral source of truth, then scaffold DesigoLogWatcher (net10.0-windows single-file) under src\ with the PRD file layout.
tasks.details:
REUSE POLICY (applies to all later tasks):
- Source of truth for behavior is Watch 0.4.0: Watch\Watch-PvssLog.ps1 + Watch\PvssRules.ps1 + Watch\ui\ + launchers + watch-config.txt.
- Reuse unchanged where possible: ui\ assets, config key set/semantics, CLI switch names/meaning, rule Ids/patterns/ranking, snapshot/report shapes, HTTP paths/methods/JSON keys.
- Rewrite only the host: C# exe, hot-path I/O/parsing (spans, compiled regex), packaging. Do not redesign detections or invent alternate APIs/log formats.
- Port algorithms by citing the PS function (and line range when known). Do not invent header formats, severity aliases, lifecycle phrases, or /api routes.

NON-GOALS for 0.5.0 (do not implement): Blazor/SPA rewrite; cross-platform; Findings window-scaling; startup-plume tagging; absolute dashboard From/To; chart ladder; Detections UI polish; catch-up % feel tuning; dual-render unify (→ 0.5.1 / Ideas). Entire-window cache only if T12 measurement warrants it (PRD §4.6).

5A DELIVERABLES:
1) Inventory doc (under docs\ or .taskmaster\docs\) covering: all CLI params; all watch-config keys + validation ranges; every HTTP route+method+body/query (including POST /api/control actions and POST /api/logPath); hand-written analysis vs rule-table map; PS function → planned C# type/file map; log auto-discovery order; ui\ static paths.
2) Scaffold src\DesigoLogWatcher\DesigoLogWatcher.csproj per PRD §6.1 (net10.0-windows, PublishSingleFile, SelfContained, win-x64, IncludeNativeLibrariesForSelfExtract) + empty Program.cs and placeholder files listed in §4.1.
3) Confirm operator exe name DesigoLogWatcher.exe; publish recipe: dotnet publish src\DesigoLogWatcher\DesigoLogWatcher.csproj -c Release -o Watch\
tasks.testStrategy: dotnet build + publish to Watch\ produces runnable DesigoLogWatcher.exe. Inventory lists every /api route found by searching Watch-PvssLog.ps1 (must include /api/health, /api/pulse, /api/section, /api/manager, /api/snapshot, /api/control, /api/logPath). Placeholder sources compile. No behavior changes yet.

subtasks.title: Inventory 0.4.0: CLI, config, APIs, hand-written analysis, and reuse map
subtasks.description: Produce the 5A inventory that later tasks must follow: contracts from Watch-PvssLog.ps1 / PvssRules.ps1, not invented alternatives.
subtasks.details:
Read Watch\Watch-PvssLog.ps1 and Watch\PvssRules.ps1 and write an inventory that includes:
- CLI: full param block (LogPath, Port, LastMinutes, RefreshSeconds, NoBrowser, NoPause, TopN, SamplePerPattern ValidateRange 0-5, SampleMaxChars, Report, OutPath, Format, Organize All|Severity|Driver, Severities, Areas, Driver, Entire, From, To, LastHours, Interactive) + dashboard-only behaviors.
- Config: Get-WatchConfigDefaults keys (14) and validation ranges from the config loader (note SamplePerPattern config validates 1-20 while CLI param is 0-5 — preserve both).
- HTTP: every route+method. Known: GET /api/health, GET /api/pulse, GET /api/section, GET /api/manager, GET /api/snapshot, POST /api/control (actions: pause, resume, restart, setWindow, note), POST /api/logPath. Capture query/body fields and JSON keys the ui\ expects.
- Rules: list all rule Ids from PvssRules.ps1 (currently 23) + Scope/BucketBy/Measure/Sample/FindingAt fields.
- Hand-written analysis outside the rule table (must be ported for parity): BACnet device Failed/OK flips + BacFlapMin findings; BACnetCollectTrend/BACnetTimeSync orchestration counters; Apogee/CoHo orchestration trio metrics; project/manager lifecycle (ReProjectUp, ReProjectShutdown, ReProjectStopped, RePmonMgrRestart, ReMgrStartProj, ReMgrStopMsg, blocking, etc.); Build-Findings; pattern/module accumulators (Add-Pattern, Normalize-Message, Ensure-Minute*).
- Map: PS function → C# file (Config.cs, Cli.cs, LogParser.cs, AnalysisState.cs, RuleEngine.cs, SnapshotBuilder.cs, ReportWriter.cs, HttpServer.cs).
- Log discovery order and FileShare.ReadWrite open semantics.
- ui\ static asset list; publish content-copy decision for ui\ into Watch\.
This inventory is the checklist for HttpServer (T9) and analysis ports (T5–T7). Do not invent routes or formats.
subtasks.testStrategy: Inventory is complete if grepping Watch-PvssLog.ps1 for /api/ finds no route omitted, and hand-written blocks in Process-LogLine / Build-Findings are listed with target C# homes.

subtasks.title: Create DesigoLogWatcher.csproj with net10.0-windows and single-file publish configuration
subtasks.description: Scaffold new C# console project under src/DesigoLogWatcher with proper.csproj settings for single-file, self-contained Windows deployment targeting.NET 10.
subtasks.details: Execute 'dotnet new console -n DesigoLogWatcher -o src\DesigoLogWatcher' to generate initial project structure. Edit DesigoLogWatcher.csproj to set TargetFramework to 'net10.0-windows', OutputType to 'Exe', enable ImplicitUsings and Nullable, and configure single-file publish settings: PublishSingleFile=true, SelfContained=true, RuntimeIdentifier=win-x64, IncludeNativeLibrariesForSelfExtract=true. These settings ensure the published output is a single executable that bundles the.NET runtime and native dependencies, eliminating the need for operators to have.NET installed. Verify the.csproj matches the PRD specification exactly, as PublishSingleFile is a publish-time setting that requires specific dotnet publish invocation.
subtasks.testStrategy: Run 'dotnet build src\DesigoLogWatcher\DesigoLogWatcher.csproj' to verify the project compiles successfully and confirm that the.csproj file contains all required PropertyGroup elements with correct values by inspecting the XML structure.

subtasks.title: Configure build output to Watch/ directory with DesigoLogWatcher.exe assembly name
subtasks.description: Set up build and publish configuration to output the compiled executable to the Watch/ directory with the operator-facing binary name DesigoLogWatcher.exe.
subtasks.details: Ensure the project name 'DesigoLogWatcher' produces an assembly named 'DesigoLogWatcher.exe' by default, or explicitly set <AssemblyName>DesigoLogWatcher</AssemblyName> in the.csproj PropertyGroup. Document the publish recipe 'dotnet publish src\DesigoLogWatcher\DesigoLogWatcher.csproj -c Release -o Watch\' that places the single-file self-contained executable directly into the Watch folder alongside the existing PowerShell runtime. Verify that this publish command produces DesigoLogWatcher.exe in the Watch/ directory without requiring additional build configuration or post-build copy steps. This layout maintains the field package structure where Watch/ contains all runtime components and the package root holds only launchers and documentation.
subtasks.testStrategy: Execute the documented publish command and verify that Watch\DesigoLogWatcher.exe is created, check that the file size indicates single-file bundling (should be substantially larger than a framework-dependent build), and confirm the executable runs without errors by invoking it directly from the command line.

subtasks.title: Create placeholder source files for all major analyzer components
subtasks.description: Establish initial source file structure with empty placeholder classes for Config, LogParser, RuleEngine, AnalysisState, SnapshotBuilder, ReportWriter, HttpServer, and Cli components.
subtasks.details: Create src\DesigoLogWatcher\Config.cs with an empty Config class stubbed for configuration loading, src\DesigoLogWatcher\LogParser.cs for log file streaming and parsing, src\DesigoLogWatcher\RuleEngine.cs for rule detection logic, src\DesigoLogWatcher\AnalysisState.cs for state management, src\DesigoLogWatcher\SnapshotBuilder.cs for JSON snapshot generation, src\DesigoLogWatcher\ReportWriter.cs for HTML/text report output, src\DesigoLogWatcher\HttpServer.cs for dashboard API server, and src\DesigoLogWatcher\Cli.cs for command-line argument parsing. Create a src\DesigoLogWatcher\Rules\ subdirectory to hold future rule implementations. Each file should contain a minimal namespace and class declaration with TODO comments indicating their future purpose, ensuring the project compiles but deferring all business logic to subsequent implementation phases.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify all placeholder files exist in the expected locations, run 'dotnet build' to confirm the project compiles successfully with empty class declarations, and check that the Rules\ subdirectory is present and ready for future rule files.

subtasks.title: Validate build and publish produces runnable self-contained executable without.NET runtime dependency
subtasks.description: Perform end-to-end validation that the scaffolded project builds, publishes to Watch/, and produces a working self-contained executable that runs on systems without.NET installed.
subtasks.details: Execute 'dotnet build src\DesigoLogWatcher\DesigoLogWatcher.csproj' to verify development build succeeds, then run 'dotnet publish src\DesigoLogWatcher\DesigoLogWatcher.csproj -c Release -o Watch\' to generate the single-file self-contained package. Launch Watch\DesigoLogWatcher.exe directly from the command line to confirm it executes without requiring a global.NET runtime installation, validating that the single-file bundling correctly packages all dependencies. Update Program.cs with a minimal entry point that prints version information and exits cleanly, providing a hook for future mode selection (dashboard vs report) and CLI argument processing. Document the successful scaffold in development notes, confirming that the baseline structure is ready for incremental feature implementation in subsequent phases without requiring project reorganization.
subtasks.testStrategy: On a test machine without.NET SDK or runtime installed, copy Watch\DesigoLogWatcher.exe and execute it to verify it runs independently. Check that the executable prints expected output and exits with code 0, confirming the self-contained publish worked correctly and all native libraries are properly extracted and loaded.

tasks.title: Config.cs implementation for watch-config.txt load, validation, and self-correction
tasks.description: Implement the configuration subsystem that loads watch-config.txt, validates and self-corrects configuration values, and applies precedence rules between file-based settings and CLI overrides while preserving 0.4.x behavior.
tasks.testStrategy: Develop unit tests for the Config loader that feed synthetic watch-config.txt files containing valid, invalid, and borderline values, asserting that valid keys are parsed correctly and invalid ones are reset to defaults while producing appropriate console messages. Add tests that simulate CLI overrides, verifying that CLI-provided values take precedence over file-based settings and that report mode does not modify LogPath while dashboard mode may update it according to the PRD’s rules. Use file-system-based tests to confirm that self-correction rewrites the config file on disk, preserving comments where possible and only adjusting invalid value lines, and exercise reload behavior to ensure that an updated watch-config.txt is reflected in the running configuration when the restart path is triggered.

subtasks.title: Implement key=value parser with comment and whitespace handling
subtasks.description: Create a robust configuration file parser that reads watch-config.txt line-by-line, handles comments (lines starting with #), blank lines, and splits key=value pairs while preserving exact PowerShell parsing behavior.
subtasks.details: Implement the core parsing logic that opens Watch\watch-config.txt using regular file I/O, reads each line, and filters out comments (lines starting with # after trimming) and blank/whitespace-only lines. For valid lines, split on the first '=' character to separate key from value, trimming both parts. Handle malformed lines (no '=' or empty key) by logging warnings and skipping. The parser must exactly replicate the PowerShell Read-WatchConfig function's line processing logic (lines 165-178 in Watch-PvssLog.ps1), including the IndexOf('=') approach and substring extraction. Return a raw dictionary of string key-value pairs that will be consumed by the strongly-typed WatchConfig class in the next subtask.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test the parser with synthetic watch-config.txt files containing valid key=value pairs, comment lines with and without leading whitespace, blank lines, lines with no '=' character, lines with empty keys, and lines with multiple '=' characters. Assert that comments and blanks are ignored, valid pairs are extracted correctly, and malformed lines produce appropriate warnings without throwing exceptions.

subtasks.title: Create strongly-typed WatchConfig class with validation ranges
subtasks.description: Design and implement the WatchConfig class with all 14 configuration properties (PreferredPort, MaxPortTries, RefreshSeconds, OpenBrowser, Browser, DefaultWindowMinutes, DefaultWindowEntire, DefaultSeverities, DefaultAreas, TopN, SamplePerPattern, SampleMaxChars, BacFlapMin, LogPath) including type conversion and range validation logic.
subtasks.details:
Define WatchConfig matching Get-WatchConfigDefaults (Watch-PvssLog.ps1 ~75-92): PreferredPort, MaxPortTries, RefreshSeconds, OpenBrowser, Browser, DefaultWindowMinutes, DefaultWindowEntire, DefaultSeverities, DefaultAreas, TopN, SamplePerPattern, SampleMaxChars, BacFlapMin, LogPath.
Validate using the SAME ranges as the PowerShell config loader: PreferredPort 1-65535; MaxPortTries 1-200; RefreshSeconds 1-60; DefaultWindowMinutes 1-10080; TopN 5-100; SamplePerPattern 1-20 (config file); SampleMaxChars 100-2000; BacFlapMin 1-50.
Booleans: ConvertTo-ConfigBool semantics (1|true|yes|on / 0|false|no|off).
DefaultSeverities tokens: FATAL|SEVERE|ERROR|WARNING|INFO (drop invalid, keep valid). DefaultAreas: SYS|IMPL|CTRL|PARAM|OTHER.
Browser: default|chrome|msedge|path. Collect corrections and feed self-rewrite (subtask 3).
subtasks.testStrategy: Test WatchConfig construction with dictionaries containing valid values in-range, values at boundary limits (e.g., PreferredPort=1, 65535), out-of-range integers, unparseable strings, and boolean variants (true/yes/1/on and false/no/0/off). Validate that DefaultSeverities correctly filters mixed valid/invalid tokens and preserves valid ones, and that unknown severity or area tokens are dropped with warnings. Confirm defaults are applied when parsing fails.

subtasks.title: Implement self-correction file rewrite preserving structure and comments
subtasks.description: Build the self-correction logic that rewrites watch-config.txt when invalid values are detected, updating only the incorrect key=value lines to their default values while preserving all comments, blank lines, and file structure.
subtasks.details: Implement the Set-WatchConfigKeys equivalent (lines 105-132) that accepts a dictionary of corrections (key -> corrected value). Read the existing watch-config.txt into a list of lines preserving original formatting. For each correction key, locate the line matching '^\s*{key}\s*=' using a case-sensitive search, and replace that line with the corrected 'key=formatted_value' line. If a correction key is not found in the file (should be rare), append it to the end with a blank line separator. Use Format-WatchConfigValue logic (lines 94-103) to serialize booleans as 'true'/'false' strings and arrays (DefaultSeverities, DefaultAreas) as comma-separated values. Write the corrected lines back to watch-config.txt with UTF-8 encoding, preserving the original line order and all comment/blank lines. Only invoke the rewrite when the corrections dictionary is non-empty. Emit console messages for each corrected key indicating the invalid value, reason, and reset default.
subtasks.testStrategy: Create unit tests with a watch-config.txt containing an out-of-range PreferredPort and an invalid OpenBrowser value. Run the config loader and self-correction, then re-read the file and verify that the invalid lines have been corrected to defaults while all comment lines and structure remain unchanged. Test that valid keys are not rewritten and that the file is not touched when no corrections are needed.

subtasks.title: Add CLI override precedence for command-line arguments
subtasks.description: Implement precedence logic ensuring that command-line arguments always override corresponding watch-config.txt values, replicating the existing CLI parameter system from Watch-PvssLog.ps1.
subtasks.details: After loading WatchConfig from file, merge CLI-provided arguments so that any explicitly set CLI parameter (e.g., -Port, -LogPath, -RefreshSeconds, -TopN, -SamplePerPattern, -SampleMaxChars) supersedes the file-based value. The merge must distinguish between a CLI argument not provided (use config file value) versus explicitly provided (use CLI value even if same as default). Reference the PowerShell param block (lines 13-45) and ensure that CLI switches for report mode (-Report, -OutPath, -Format, -Organize, -Severities, -Areas, -Driver, -TopN, -Entire, -LastHours, -LastMinutes, -From, -To, -Interactive, -NoPause) are integrated. For dashboard mode, CLI overrides apply to -Port (PreferredPort), -LastMinutes (DefaultWindowMinutes), -RefreshSeconds, -TopN, -SamplePerPattern, -SampleMaxChars, and -NoBrowser (inverts OpenBrowser). Ensure that the final WatchConfig object returned from the Load method reflects CLI > file precedence and that CLI overrides are not written back to the config file during self-correction.
subtasks.testStrategy: Construct tests where watch-config.txt defines PreferredPort=8787 and RefreshSeconds=5, then invoke the CLI parser with -Port 9999. Verify the resulting WatchConfig has Port=9999 and RefreshSeconds=5 (file value). Confirm that self-correction does not rewrite PreferredPort to 9999 in the file. Test -NoBrowser override against OpenBrowser=true in the file, ensuring the runtime uses NoBrowser but the file remains unchanged.

subtasks.title: Implement mode-specific LogPath write-back rules
subtasks.description: Add mode-aware LogPath update logic so that dashboard mode updates LogPath in watch-config.txt when Start is invoked, while report mode never writes back LogPath, matching 0.4.x behavior.
subtasks.details:
Dashboard Start / successful log open may persist LogPath via the Set-WatchConfigKeys equivalent. Report mode never writes LogPath.
Gate on mode flag. Prefer updating through the same self-correction rewriter so comments/order are preserved.
Wire later to POST /api/logPath and dashboard Start flows (T9/T10) — do not invent a separate /api/start route.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test dashboard mode with empty LogPath in watch-config.txt, POST /api/logPath with a concrete path, and verify LogPath is persisted. After POST /api/control action=restart (or reload), confirm LogPath is prefilled from config. Report mode with CLI -LogPath must not change config LogPath. LogPath write-back must not rewrite unrelated keys unless they are also invalid.

subtasks.title: Add runtime reload capability for dashboard restart action
subtasks.description: Enable the WatchConfig class to reload configuration from watch-config.txt at runtime when the dashboard restart API is invoked, picking up user edits without requiring a process restart.
subtasks.details:
Expose Reload()/Load that re-reads watch-config.txt, re-validates, re-applies CLI overrides. Dashboard POST /api/control action=restart calls this (same as Apply-WatchConfig -Runtime).
Preserve PS semantics: PreferredPort/MaxPortTries/OpenBrowser/Browser may require full host relaunch; runtime keys (RefreshSeconds, window defaults, filters, TopN, samples, BacFlapMin) apply after reload. Keep previous config on read failure.
subtasks.testStrategy: Start the dashboard with default config values, edit watch-config.txt to change RefreshSeconds and DefaultWindowMinutes, invoke the /api/restart endpoint, and verify that the new values are picked up and reflected in subsequent /api/pulse and window operations. Confirm that changes to PreferredPort in the file do not affect the running host (it continues on the original port) and that a console message or log entry documents the successful reload. Test reload failure by deleting or corrupting watch-config.txt mid-session and verify the dashboard continues with the prior config and logs an error.

tasks.title: Cli.cs and Program.cs: CLI parsing, mode selection, and interactive prompts
tasks.description: Implement robust command-line parsing and mode selection for dashboard and report modes, supporting all existing switches, interactive prompts, and manager pick range syntax while maintaining compatibility with 0.4.x CLI behavior.
tasks.details:
Implement Cli + Program entry: parse all existing switches with identical names/semantics. Parser may be System.CommandLine or a small hand parser (PRD §5).
Required switches: -LogPath, -OutPath, -Format (Text|Html|Both), -Organize (All|Severity|Driver), -Severities, -Areas, -Driver, -TopN, -Entire, -LastHours, -LastMinutes, -From, -To, -Interactive, -NoPause, -Report, plus dashboard -Port/-NoBrowser/-RefreshSeconds/-SamplePerPattern/-SampleMaxChars as today.
Date-only -To = end of that calendar day (PS ~620-622). Relative windows (-Entire/-LastHours/-LastMinutes) win over -From/-To.
-Interactive: Enter-defaulted prompts matching PS sequence; manager pick MUST accept range syntax 1-3,10 (§2.1) — implement here in T3.5 (T8 only verifies).
Report mode: no port bind, no browser open, no LogPath write-back; exit codes + -NoPause/pause-on-exit match launchers.
tasks.testStrategy: Construct unit tests and integration tests around the Cli and Program entry points that cover all supported switches, including combinations that exercise window precedence rules where relative windows override absolute From/To settings. Validate that -Report correctly selects report mode, that -Interactive causes the process to prompt for values instead of relying solely on arguments, and that -NoPause suppresses any end-of-run keypress wait. Create dedicated tests for the manager pick range syntax, feeding inputs such as "1", "1-3", and "1-3,10" and asserting that the resulting selection sets are accurate, ordered, and free of duplicates. Additionally, run end-to-end tests where the exe is invoked via the existing Run-Report-Interactive.cmd and Run-Watch.cmd scripts to confirm that arguments are forwarded and interpreted correctly and that help text remains readable for field operators.

subtasks.title: Design CliOptions capturing all Watch 0.4.0 switches
subtasks.description: Strongly-typed options mirroring the PowerShell param block and ValidateSet/ValidateRange constraints.
subtasks.details: Include every param from Watch-PvssLog.ps1 param() (~13-45). Organize is string enum All|Severity|Driver (NOT bool). Format is Text|Html|Both. SamplePerPattern CLI range is 0-5; config file range remains 1-20. From/To are strings/DateTime with date-only To semantics. Document relative-window precedence over absolute bounds.
subtasks.testStrategy: Create unit tests that instantiate CliOptions with various property combinations, validating type constraints, default values, and that the object correctly represents all possible CLI states from the PowerShell version. Test edge cases like null paths, zero/negative TopN, and conflicting window parameters.

subtasks.title: Implement System.CommandLine integration with RootCommand and option definitions
subtasks.description: Integrate System.CommandLine library to define a RootCommand with all option definitions, preserving exact switch names and semantics from the PowerShell CLI while generating automatic help text.
subtasks.details: If using System.CommandLine: Option types must match semantics — Organize is Option<string> with All|Severity|Driver (not Option<bool>). Format Option<string> Text|Html|Both. Switches for Entire/Interactive/NoPause/Report/NoBrowser as bool. Wire handler → CliOptions. Help text must stay operator-usable. A hand parser is equally acceptable if behavior matches.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test System.CommandLine integration by invoking the root command with various argument combinations and asserting that the resulting CliOptions object matches expected values. Test help text generation with '--help' flag. Validate that unknown switches produce appropriate error messages and that required vs optional parameters behave correctly.

subtasks.title: Implement mode selection logic branching to dashboard vs report pipelines
subtasks.description: Build the mode selection logic in Program.cs that branches execution flow into either dashboard mode (HTTP server + log tailing) or report mode (batch analysis with exit) based on the -Report flag and interactive inputs.
subtasks.details: In Program.cs Main method, invoke the Cli parser to obtain a CliOptions instance. Implement branching logic: if CliOptions.Report is true, call RunReportMode(config, options); otherwise call RunDashboardMode(config, options). Define RunReportMode as a method that loads configuration, applies CLI overrides, executes the full analysis pipeline, writes output files, and exits the process. Define RunDashboardMode as a method that loads configuration, applies overrides, starts the HttpServer instance, and begins log tailing with periodic re-analysis. Ensure both pipelines respect CLI overrides for paths, windows, and formatting options by merging CliOptions into the Config object before analysis.
subtasks.testStrategy: Create integration tests that launch Program.Main with different argument sets: one with -Report flag to verify report mode execution and process exit, another without -Report to verify dashboard mode starts (mock HttpServer to avoid binding). Assert that correct pipeline methods are invoked and that configuration merging produces expected analysis parameters.

subtasks.title: Implement interactive prompt system for -Interactive mode with Enter-defaulted answers
subtasks.description: Build an interactive prompt system that presents questions to users when -Interactive flag is set, supporting Enter-defaulted answers and replicating the 0.4.0 PowerShell host behavior for report mode parameter collection.
subtasks.details: Create an InteractivePrompt class with methods for each configurable parameter: PromptForLogPath(defaultValue), PromptForOutputPath(defaultValue), PromptForFormat(defaultValue), PromptForOrganize(defaultValue), PromptForWindow(defaultValues), PromptForFilters(defaultValues). Each prompt method should display the question text, show the default value in brackets [default], read Console.ReadLine(), and return the default if input is empty/whitespace or parse the input otherwise. Implement validation and re-prompting for invalid inputs. Wire these prompts into the CLI parsing flow: when -Interactive is true, call prompt methods to populate/override CliOptions properties before proceeding to mode selection. Mirror the PowerShell prompt sequence and phrasing exactly.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test interactive prompts by mocking Console input/output streams and feeding sequences of user inputs (empty lines for defaults, valid values, invalid values requiring re-prompt). Assert that the resulting CliOptions object contains expected values from prompts and that default handling works correctly. Verify prompt text matches PowerShell version.

subtasks.title: Build manager pick range parser supporting syntax '1-3,10' with validation
subtasks.description: Implement a robust parser for manager pick range syntax that handles comma-separated tokens, range expansion, deduplication, validation against actual manager lists, and interactive selection UI for -Interactive mode.
subtasks.details: Implement ParseManagerRange("1-3,10") → distinct sorted ints; reject malformed input; integrate into -Interactive manager pick. This fulfills the §2.1 manager-range exception (T8.5 is verification only).
subtasks.testStrategy: Write unit tests for ParseRangeString with inputs like '1', '1,3,5', '1-3', '1-3,10', '5-5', '10-1' (invalid), 'abc' (invalid), '1-3,2-4' (overlapping/dedup), and '999' (out of bounds). Assert correct expansion, deduplication, and validation. Test InteractiveManagerPick with mocked console I/O for complete selection workflows including re-prompts on error.

subtasks.title: Implement window precedence rules where relative windows override absolute From/To
subtasks.description: Implement the window precedence logic that ensures relative window parameters (-Entire, -LastHours, -LastMinutes) take precedence over absolute window parameters (-From, -To) when both are specified.
subtasks.details: Add a ResolveWindowPrecedence() method to CliOptions or Cli class that applies precedence rules: if -Entire is true, set window to entire log and clear From/To; else if -LastHours or -LastMinutes is set, calculate relative window from current time and clear From/To; else use From/To if both are set; else default to appropriate window (LastHours=24 or entire log based on mode). Document this logic clearly in code comments matching the PowerShell behavior. Ensure that Config merging applies these rules consistently so that the analysis pipeline receives unambiguous window parameters. Return a normalized TimeWindow object with explicit Start/End DateTimes or an EntireLog flag.
subtasks.testStrategy: Create unit tests with CliOptions instances containing various window parameter combinations: Entire only, LastHours only, From+To only, Entire+From+To (Entire wins), LastHours+From+To (LastHours wins), no window params (defaults). Assert that ResolveWindowPrecedence returns correct TimeWindow objects matching PowerShell behavior. Test in both dashboard and report mode contexts.

subtasks.title: Generate help text and integrate Cli with Program.cs entry point
subtasks.description: Complete the CLI integration by generating comprehensive help text, integrating the Cli class with Program.cs Main method, and ensuring operator-friendly usage messages that match existing documentation and preserve workflow compatibility.
subtasks.details: Enhance System.CommandLine option definitions with detailed descriptions for help text generation. Add examples and usage notes to the RootCommand description showing common invocations: dashboard mode (no args), report mode with -Report, interactive mode with -Interactive, window selection examples, and manager pick syntax. Integrate Cli.BuildRootCommand() into Program.cs Main: parse args, invoke command handler, handle return codes. Add global exception handling around CLI parsing to catch and display user-friendly error messages. Ensure that invoking with --help or invalid arguments produces clear, operator-friendly output. Test that existing Run-Watch.cmd and Run-Report.cmd batch launchers work unchanged with the new DesigoLogWatcher.exe by updating their target executable name.
subtasks.testStrategy: Execute the compiled DesigoLogWatcher.exe with --help flag and verify output includes all switches with descriptions and examples. Test with invalid arguments and assert friendly error messages. Run existing batch launchers (updated to call.exe) and verify they produce expected behavior. Conduct operator acceptance testing with representatives familiar with 0.4.x CLI to confirm workflow compatibility.

tasks.title: LogParser.cs: high-performance streaming read, windowing, and tailing
tasks.description: Implement a high-performance log parser that can stream PVSS_II.log with shared read access, efficiently enumerate lines using spans, apply analysis windows, and support both catch-up and tailing for dashboard and report modes.
tasks.details:
LogParser: open with FileAccess.Read + FileShare.ReadWrite; stream lines (do not load whole file); windowing Entire/LastHours/LastMinutes/From/To (date-only To = end of day); catch-up + tail for dashboard; detect truncation/rotation.
Hot path: prefer ReadOnlySpan<char>, reuse buffers; avoid per-line LINQ / unnecessary string copies (PRD §3).
Header field extraction belongs with AnalysisState/T5 using the real LineRe — LogParser provides lines/bytes/progress.
Perf: instrument here; <5s / <1s on ~50MB are aspirations (PRD §9.1), not hard ship blockers — final numbers + cache decision live in T12.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit/integration tests for shared-read open, window bounds (including date-only To), catch-up then tail, truncation detect. Record parse timings for T12; do not fail CI solely for exceeding 5s.

subtasks.title: Implement FileStream with concurrent read access using FileShare.ReadWrite
subtasks.description: Open PVSS_II.log with FileAccess.Read and FileShare.ReadWrite so Desigo CC / WinCC OA can keep appending.
subtasks.details: FileStream FileMode.Open, FileAccess.Read, FileShare.ReadWrite. Handle missing/access errors. Track length/position for streaming. Match 0.4.0 live-log safety — no exclusive lock.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests that verify FileStream opens successfully with correct sharing mode. Integration tests with a simulated log writer appending lines concurrently while LogParser reads. Validate that both processes can access the file simultaneously without locking errors.

subtasks.title: Design buffered line enumeration using ReadOnlySpan<char> for zero-allocation parsing
subtasks.description: Implement efficient line enumeration that reads file in buffered chunks and yields ReadOnlySpan<char> per line to eliminate per-line substring allocations.
subtasks.details: Create an internal method EnumerateLines that reads the log file in large buffered chunks (e.g., 64KB-256KB) using the FileStream from task 1. Use StreamReader with custom buffer size, reading lines and converting to ReadOnlySpan<char> via.AsSpan() to avoid allocating new strings for every line. Handle edge cases including very long lines (>2000 chars), empty lines, lines with only whitespace, and buffer boundaries that split lines. Implement span-based parsing for timestamp extraction (YYYY.MM.DD HH:mm:ss.fff), severity level detection (SEVERE, WARNING, INFO), and module identification without creating intermediate string objects. Use stackalloc for small temporary buffers where appropriate.
subtasks.testStrategy: Performance tests comparing allocation profiles (measuring Gen0/Gen1/Gen2 collections) between span-based and traditional string parsing on 50MB corpus. Unit tests with synthetic logs containing edge cases: empty lines, very long lines (10KB+), lines with various PVSS_II.log header formats. Validate correct line boundaries and no data loss at buffer edges.

subtasks.title: Implement analysis window logic for Entire, LastHours, LastMinutes, From, and To
subtasks.description: Build windowing logic that computes timestamp boundaries and filters lines to requested time ranges, supporting all five window modes with proper precedence.
subtasks.details: Implement AnalysisWindow abstraction with five modes: Entire (full file), LastHours (relative to current time or log end), LastMinutes (relative), From (absolute start), and To (absolute end). Compute timestamp boundaries before enumeration begins, using file metadata (creation/modification times) and first/last line timestamps to optimize seeking. For relative windows (LastHours/LastMinutes), calculate cutoff timestamp and skip lines until the window start is reached. For absolute windows (From/To), parse and compare line timestamps against boundaries. Apply CLI precedence rules where relative windows (-LastHours/-LastMinutes) override absolute -From/-To settings when both are specified. Implement efficient seeking for large files: for Entire mode start at file beginning, for recent windows consider starting near file end and working backward or using binary search on timestamps if log is chronological.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests exercising each window mode independently with known synthetic logs. Tests validating precedence rules when multiple window switches are combined. Performance tests measuring window application overhead on 50MB corpus. Edge case tests for logs spanning midnight, logs with non-monotonic timestamps, and empty window results.

subtasks.title: Build catch-up phase with historical window processing and progress tracking
subtasks.description: Catch-up over the analysis window with progress % hooks for dashboard (T10 wires to /api/pulse|/api/health).
subtasks.details: Process historical window once; expose progress percentage + message for Sync-equivalent state. Do not bind HTTP here — T10 integrates. Process each in-window line exactly once before tail.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration tests that simulate catch-up on logs of various sizes (1MB, 10MB, 50MB) and verify progress percentages are reported correctly. Tests validating that all lines in the window are processed exactly once. Performance tests measuring catch-up time on 50MB corpus to validate aspirational sub-5-second timing (aspirational sub-1-second). Mock AnalysisState/RuleEngine to isolate catch-up logic.

subtasks.title: Implement tailing loop with file position monitoring and new byte detection
subtasks.description: Build tailing mode that monitors log file for new appended bytes, reads and processes new lines in near real-time for dashboard live updates.
subtasks.details: After catch-up completes (task 4), transition to tailing loop that periodically checks if file size has grown beyond the last-read position. Use FileStream.Length or FileInfo.Length to detect new bytes without re-opening the file. When new bytes detected, read from last_position to new end, enumerate new lines using the span-based parsing from task 2, and feed them to AnalysisState/RuleEngine. Implement polling interval (e.g., 500ms-2000ms, configurable) to balance responsiveness vs CPU overhead. For dashboard mode, new lines update the live state and trigger /api/pulse updates for UI refresh. Handle the case where no new bytes appear for extended periods gracefully (no busy-wait). Maintain file position cursor accurately across iterations. Tailing runs indefinitely in dashboard mode until user pauses or stops.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration tests with a background thread or process appending lines to a log file while LogParser tails, verifying all new lines are detected and processed. Tests measuring tail latency: time from line written to line processed. Tests validating polling interval is respected and CPU usage remains low during idle periods (no new lines).

subtasks.title: Add log rotation and truncation detection with re-seeking logic
subtasks.description: Implement resilience to log rotation or truncation by detecting file size shrink and re-seeking from the beginning when PVSS_II.log is reset.
subtasks.details: In the tailing loop (task 5), before reading new bytes, compare current file size with last-known size. If file size has decreased (indicating truncation or rotation), log a warning/info message and reset the file position to 0 (beginning of file). Re-initialize catch-up from the start of the (now smaller/new) log file, re-processing lines as if starting fresh. Optionally clear or reset AnalysisState aggregates to avoid stale data from the previous log mixing with the new log, depending on product requirements (consult dashboard behavior in 0.4.0 for precedent). Handle edge case where file size stays the same but content changed (rare; inode/file handle change detection may require re-opening the file). Ensure robust error handling for file access issues during rotation (file temporarily unavailable).
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration tests that simulate log rotation by truncating the log file mid-tail, then appending new lines, verifying LogParser detects shrink and re-processes from beginning. Tests that replace the log file entirely (delete and create new) and verify the parser adapts. Edge case tests for simultaneous rotation and append operations.

subtasks.title: Optimize span-based timestamp, severity, and module parsing to avoid allocations
subtasks.description: Refine line parsing to extract timestamps, severity levels, and module names using span slicing and pattern matching without creating substring allocations.
subtasks.details: Timestamp/severity/module extraction for windowing may stay minimal here; authoritative LineRe parse is T5. Prefer spans/buffers; avoid unnecessary string copies. Do not invent bracket-style headers.
subtasks.testStrategy: Microbenchmarks comparing span-based parsing vs traditional string parsing for representative PVSS_II.log lines, measuring allocations (bytes allocated per operation) and throughput (lines/sec). Unit tests validating correct extraction of timestamp, severity, and module fields from various log line formats, including edge cases (missing fields, malformed headers). Validate that no intermediate string allocations occur during parsing hot path using a memory profiler.

subtasks.title: Add parse instrumentation (aspirational <5s on ~50MB)
subtasks.description: Measure catch-up/parse phases on the ~50MB corpus; record numbers for T12. No hard fail on >5s.
subtasks.details: Stopwatch key phases. Record results for PROGRESS later. Optimize obvious hotspots if multi-minute, but do not treat <5s as a release gate (PRD §9.1). Cache decision is T12 only.
subtasks.testStrategy: Instrumentation runs and prints/records timings. Document measured times; no CI fail solely for exceeding 5s.

tasks.title: AnalysisState.cs and header parsing: pattern, module, and lifecycle accumulation
tasks.description: Port Process-LogLine header parse + AnalysisState accumulators (including hand-written BACnet/Apogee/lifecycle analysis) for snapshot/rule inputs — behavioral match to 0.4.0.
tasks.details:
Port header parse + AnalysisState accumulators from Process-LogLine and helpers. SOURCE OF TRUTH: Watch-PvssLog.ps1 LineRe and Process-LogLine — do not invent bracket-log formats.

LineRe (exact):
 ^([^,]+),\s*(\d{4}\.\d{2}\.\d{2}\s+\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}\.\d+),\s*([^,]+),\s*([^,\s]+)
Groups: component, timestamp, area, severity.

Severity: ToUpperInvariant; only alias WARN→WARNING. Categories used: FATAL|SEVERE|ERROR|WARNING|INFO (no DEBUG/CRITICAL invention).

Must port hand-written analysis (PRD §4.5), not stub: BACnet Failed/OK flips + object-list; BACnetCollectTrend/TimeSync; CoHo stuck; Apogee orchestration metrics; lifecycle regexes (ReProjectUp='The project is up and running', ReProjectStopped, ReProjectShutdown, ReProjectStartMode, RePmonMgrRestart, ReMgrStartProj, ReMgrStopMsg, ReDriverReady, ReBlockingStart/End); Add-Pattern/Normalize-Message/Ensure-Minute*; Get-PerfCategory. Build-Findings can live here or SnapshotBuilder but must match 0.4.0.
tasks.testStrategy: Fixture lines matching real PVSS_II headers parse identically to PS. Aggregates on a fixed fixture match 0.4.0 exports for severities, components, lifecycle counters, BACnet flip maps — exact counts, not soft ±1 tolerance.

subtasks.title: Design AnalysisState class with accumulator structure
subtasks.description: Create the AnalysisState class to hold aggregated log analysis data including severity counts, module metrics, driver statistics, pattern tables, and lifecycle signals matching PowerShell 0.4.0 semantics.
subtasks.details: Design AnalysisState to mirror New-AnalysisData / Sync['Data'] fields used by Process-LogLine and Build-SnapshotObject in 0.4.0 (from T1.1 inventory): Severity counts keyed FATAL|SEVERE|ERROR|WARNING|INFO (not DEBUG); AreaCounts; Components/CompSev; PatternsBySev/Area/Comp + samples/times; minute buckets; BACnet flip maps; orchestration counters; lifecycle counters/events; Apogee/CoHo fields; UnparsedLines/ParsedLines/FirstTs/LastTs; etc. Prefer the inventory field list over inventing a green-field schema. Structure for streaming updates and SnapshotBuilder consumption; consider concurrency for dashboard tail.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests: default init; increment FATAL/SEVERE/… counters; fields required by SnapshotBuilder present. Compare field names against T1.1 inventory / PS New-AnalysisData.

subtasks.title: Implement LineRe-compatible header parser
subtasks.description: Parse component, timestamp, area, severity from PVSS_II.log lines using the 0.4.0 LineRe shape (span-friendly).
subtasks.details: Port $script:LineRe. Prefer span/regex-on-span; allocate strings when entering long-lived maps. Unparsed lines increment UnparsedLines like PS. Do NOT use invented formats such as "[2026-06-19 10:00:00] [ERROR] ManagerX:".
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests with real-shaped lines: "WCCOAfoo, 2026.09.04 12:00:00.123, SYS, WARNING, rest...". Malformed lines → unparsed.

subtasks.title: Severity normalization matching Process-LogLine
subtasks.description: WARN→WARNING only; keep FATAL|SEVERE|ERROR|WARNING|INFO.
subtasks.details: Match Process-LogLine (~995-996): Trim + ToUpperInvariant; if WARN then WARNING. Do not invent DEBUG/INFORMATION/CRITICAL/ERR mappings unless proven present in 0.4.0.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests verifying normalization of all expected severity aliases ('WARN'→'WARNING', 'ERR'→'ERROR', 'FATAL'→'SEVERE') and case-insensitive matching, asserting that unrecognized values default to 'INFO' and all LogEntry objects have standardized severity strings.

subtasks.title: Build pattern accumulation logic for module and driver tables
subtasks.description: Implement pattern recognition and accumulation that updates per-module and per-driver pattern tables by identifying recurring message signatures and incrementing occurrence counts in AnalysisState.
subtasks.details: Port Add-Pattern + Normalize-Message (+ Ensure-Minute*) behavior for PatternsBySev/Area/Comp and samples/time maps. Pattern keys come from Normalize-Message on the line — do not invent a new signature scheme. Respect SamplePerPattern limits.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests feeding sequences of LogEntry objects with repeated message patterns (same signature with varying dynamic values) and verifying that pattern tables correctly increment counts, aggregate by module/driver, and maintain frequency rankings matching PowerShell baseline behavior.

subtasks.title: Implement lifecycle event detection for project and manager events
subtasks.description: Add lifecycle event detection that identifies project start/stop and manager restart signatures in PVSS_II.log messages and records them in AnalysisState for snapshot building and rule evaluation.
subtasks.details: Port lifecycle detection using the named regexes already in Watch-PvssLog.ps1 (~748-758), not invented English phrases. Update the same counters/collections Process-LogLine updates (ProjectUp/Shutdown/Stopped, PmonMgrRestart, MgrStart/Stop, blocking, ProjectRestartEvents cap 200, etc.).
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests with synthetic log entries containing known lifecycle event messages (project start/stop, manager restart signatures from PVSS_II.log examples) and verifying that DetectLifecycleEvent correctly identifies events, extracts metadata, and updates AnalysisState collections and counters accurately.

subtasks.title: Port hand-written analysis (BACnet flips, orchestration, Apogee, Findings inputs)
subtasks.description: Required 0.4.0 parity work — these already exist in PowerShell and must fire under the dev gate.
subtasks.details: Port from Process-LogLine / related helpers (inventory from T1.1): BacFailed/Ok flips + BacFlapMin; BACnetCollectTrend/TimeSync command metrics; CoHo discovery stuck; Apogee PPCL/orch metrics; ApogeeDrv line counts; blocking managers; any other non-rule-table accumulators. Findings text assembly may be SnapshotBuilder but inputs must match. DO NOT stub or defer past the T7 dev gate.

subtasks.title: Validate against PowerShell Process-LogLine behavior for parity
subtasks.description: Perform end-to-end validation comparing C# header parsing and AnalysisState accumulation outputs against PowerShell 0.4.0 Process-LogLine results on representative PVSS_II.log corpus to ensure functional parity.
subtasks.details: Compare C# vs PS 0.4.0 on a fixed corpus for severity/component/pattern/lifecycle/BACnet aggregates. Fail on unexpected diffs. Soft ±1 tolerances are not acceptable for the parity gate.
subtasks.testStrategy: Automated export+diff; unexpected differences fail the test.

tasks.title: RuleEngine.cs and Rules table port: single-scope dev gate (23 rules)
tasks.description: Port the PowerShell rule table into a C# data-driven RuleEngine and Rules definitions, implementing single-scope semantics equivalent to 0.4.0 as the dev gate before enabling multi-scope and BACnet-specific extensions.
tasks.details:
Port all shipping rules from PvssRules.ps1 into RuleDefinition + data-driven RuleEngine (one row + one test). Currently 23 rule Ids (not "40+"): cns.resolveNodes, cns.reducedFunction, cns.icns, cns.tryRenew, apogeeDrv.trendOverflow, apogeeDrv.trendSeq, apogeeDrv.alertId, apogeeDrv.queryTimeout, apogeeDrv.getDataFail, state.unexpected, trend.dataLoss, trend.seqLess, driver.errorCode, driver.offline, driver.readFile, alarm.alertIdUnknown, alarm.getSummaryFail, device.cptFailed, device.aesDecrypt, afw.traceRepetition, afw.covBurst, afw.serverSideException, afw.retainedInvocations.
Dev gate: single-scope semantics exactly as Register-RuleSet (Scope substring IndexOf on component). Multi-scope + new BACnet-scoped families stay OFF until T8.
Hand-written analysis is owned by T5 — engine consumes its state; do not stub those behaviors here.
Compiled Regex, reuse for process lifetime. BucketBy/Measure/Sample/FindingAt/PatternGroup per PS hashtables.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit tests for RuleEngine + fixture parity vs 0.4.0 under single-scope dev gate (Ids, counts, ranking). Adding a rule remains one data row + one test.

subtasks.title: Design and implement RuleDefinition record structure
subtasks.description: Create a strongly-typed C# RuleDefinition record that captures all rule attributes from PowerShell PvssRules.ps1 including Id, Group, Label, Scope, Pattern (Regex), BucketBy specifications, Measure aggregations, Sample configuration, SampleSlot, FindingAt thresholds, and PatternGroup for legacy module cards.
subtasks.details: Define RuleDefinition as a sealed record with properties: string Id, string Group, string Label, string? Scope, Regex Pattern, Dictionary<string, BucketSpec>? BucketBy, Dictionary<string, MeasureSpec>? Measure, bool Sample, string? SampleSlot, int? FindingAt, string? PatternGroup. Create supporting types: BucketSpec (supports capture group index, variable names like '$component'/'$area'/'$severity', and TrimEnd modifiers via either an int Group field or string variable field, plus optional char[] TrimEnd), and MeasureSpec (int Group, string Agg with values 'Sum' or 'Max'). Ensure the structure mirrors the PowerShell hashtable format while providing compile-time type safety and null safety for optional fields.
subtasks.testStrategy: Write unit tests that instantiate RuleDefinition instances with various combinations of required and optional fields, verifying that the record accepts valid configurations (e.g., with/without Scope, with/without BucketBy containing both capture-group and variable specs, with/without Measure containing Sum/Max aggregations) and that the type system enforces required fields at compile time.

subtasks.title: Port all 23 rule definitions from PvssRules.ps1
subtasks.description: Translate every shipping rule Id into RuleDefinition data (single-scope as in 0.4.0).
subtasks.details: Create Rules data (C# records and/or checked-in data file). Port all 23 Ids with patterns, Scope, BucketBy (incl. TrimEnd / $component|$area|$severity), Measure Sum/Max, Sample/SampleSlot, FindingAt, groups. Preserve curated module card vs generic detections pipeline. Verify count against PvssRules.ps1 during T1 inventory — if repo gains rules, port those too.
subtasks.testStrategy: Create unit tests that verify the ported rule count matches the PowerShell count (23 rules), that each rule's Id, Group, Label, and Scope match the original definitions, that all regex patterns compile successfully with RegexOptions.Compiled, and that complex rules like apogeeDrv.trendOverflow and afw.traceRepetition have correctly structured BucketBy and Measure dictionaries with proper TrimEnd and aggregation settings.

subtasks.title: Implement data-driven RuleEngine processing LogEntry events
subtasks.description: Build a RuleEngine class that consumes an IReadOnlyList<RuleDefinition> and processes LogEntry events against the rule table, applying pattern matching, scope filtering, and accumulating hits into an AnalysisState structure that tracks Hits, HitSevs, HitTime, HitSample, HitBuckets, and HitMeasures dictionaries.
subtasks.details: Implement RuleEngine with a constructor accepting IReadOnlyList<RuleDefinition> and a Process(LogEntry entry, AnalysisState state) method. Introduce AnalysisState as a class with dictionaries: Hits (Dictionary<string, int>), HitSevs (Dictionary<string, Dictionary<string, int>>), HitTime (Dictionary<string, TimeSpan>), HitSample (Dictionary<string, string>), HitBuckets (Dictionary<string, Dictionary<string, Dictionary<string, int>>>), HitMeasures (Dictionary<string, Dictionary<string, double>>). In Process, iterate through _rules, apply Pattern.IsMatch(entry.Message), check Scope filter using entry.Component.IndexOf(rule.Scope, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) >= 0 if Scope is not null, and on match call a private AddRuleHit method. Implement RuleSetCache as a Dictionary<string, RuleDefinition[]> to cache component-filtered rule subsets (mirroring PowerShell Register-RuleSet function at lines 194-205). Set RuleBucketCap constant to 2000 to prevent unbounded bucket growth.
subtasks.testStrategy: Develop unit tests that instantiate RuleEngine with a small set of synthetic rules (e.g., one scoped, one unscoped, one with BucketBy, one with Measure) and process mock LogEntry instances, asserting that AnalysisState.Hits increments correctly, that scoped rules only fire for matching components, that unscoped rules fire for all entries, and that the RuleSetCache correctly filters rules by component on first access and reuses the cached ruleset on subsequent accesses.

subtasks.title: Implement compiled Regex initialization for all pattern-based rules
subtasks.description: Ensure all RuleDefinition Pattern fields are compiled Regex instances initialized at rule definition time using RegexOptions.Compiled | RegexOptions.CultureInvariant to reduce runtime overhead and reuse them across the process lifetime, matching PowerShell's [regex] type casting behavior.
subtasks.details: When constructing each RuleDefinition in the ported Rules.cs, instantiate Regex with new Regex(pattern, RegexOptions.Compiled | RegexOptions.CultureInvariant) for all pattern strings. Verify that case-insensitive patterns in PowerShell (e.g., '(?i)ResolveNodes', '(?i)Trend buffer overflow') are correctly translated using RegexOptions.IgnoreCase in addition to Compiled and CultureInvariant. Store the compiled Regex instances directly in the RuleDefinition record's Pattern property so that every call to Pattern.IsMatch or Pattern.Match in the RuleEngine reuses the pre-compiled state machine, avoiding per-match compilation costs.
subtasks.testStrategy: Write unit tests that measure the performance difference between compiled and non-compiled regex patterns on a representative sample of 1000+ log lines, confirming that compiled patterns provide measurable speedup. Add tests that verify case-insensitive patterns (e.g., 'ResolveNodes' matching 'resolvenodes') work correctly with RegexOptions.IgnoreCase, and that culture-invariant matching behaves consistently across different system locales.

subtasks.title: Implement BucketBy logic with capture groups, variables, and TrimEnd modifiers
subtasks.description: Build the GetRuleBucketValue and AddRuleHit logic that extracts bucket keys from regex Match objects using capture group indices, supports variable substitution for '$component', '$area', '$severity', applies TrimEnd character trimming, and populates AnalysisState.HitBuckets dictionaries while enforcing the RuleBucketCap limit.
subtasks.details: Implement a private GetRuleBucketValue(BucketSpec spec, Match match, string component, string area, string severity) method in RuleEngine that handles three cases: (1) spec contains a string variable ('$component', '$area', '$severity') and returns the corresponding LogEntry field; (2) spec contains an integer Group and extracts match.Groups[Group].Value.Trim(); (3) spec contains TrimEnd char[] and applies val.TrimEnd(spec.TrimEnd) after extraction. In AddRuleHit, iterate rule.BucketBy entries, call GetRuleBucketValue for each bucket name, and populate state.HitBuckets[ruleId][bucketName][value]++ while checking bm.Count < RuleBucketCap before adding new keys (mirroring PowerShell logic at lines 260-274). Set capped flag when bucket reaches cap.
subtasks.testStrategy: Create unit tests for GetRuleBucketValue that exercise all three extraction modes: (1) variable substitution returning component/area/severity from LogEntry; (2) capture group extraction from regex Match with successful and unsuccessful groups; (3) TrimEnd modifier removing trailing characters (e.g., '.' from 'Device123.'). Test AddRuleHit with rules having single and multiple bucket dimensions, verifying that distinct values are counted correctly and that the RuleBucketCap prevents unbounded growth when presented with 2000+ distinct values.

subtasks.title: Build Measure aggregation with Sum and Max operations
subtasks.description: Implement Measure metric extraction and aggregation logic that parses numeric values from regex capture groups and applies Sum or Max aggregation operations as specified in MeasureSpec, populating AnalysisState.HitMeasures dictionaries to support rules like afw.traceRepetition and afw.covBurst with dual measures.
subtasks.details: In the AddRuleHit method, add logic to process rule.Measure dictionary: for each measure name, extract the numeric value from match.Groups[spec.Group].Value using double.TryParse, and apply aggregation based on spec.Agg: if 'Sum' then state.HitMeasures[ruleId][measureName] += num, if 'Max' then state.HitMeasures[ruleId][measureName] = Math.Max(current, num), initializing to zero or the first value as appropriate (mirroring PowerShell logic at lines 277-294). Ensure that rules with multiple measures (e.g., afw.traceRepetition has 'repeats' Sum and 'worstRun' Max) are handled correctly by iterating all measure specs.
subtasks.testStrategy: Develop unit tests that define rules with Sum and Max measures, process LogEntry sequences with varying numeric capture values, and assert that Sum measures accumulate correctly (e.g., processing '10', '20', '30' yields 60) and Max measures retain the highest value (e.g., processing '10', '30', '20' yields 30). Test the afw.traceRepetition and afw.covBurst dual-measure rules with synthetic log entries to verify both aggregations run in parallel.

subtasks.title: Add Sample and SampleSlot tracking for first-match capture
subtasks.description: Implement Sample and SampleSlot logic that captures the first matching log line for each rule (or shared slot) and stores it in AnalysisState.HitSample, supporting use cases where multiple rules share a single sample slot (e.g., apogeeDrv.trendOverflow and apogeeDrv.trendSeq sharing 'apogeeDrv.trend').
subtasks.details: In AddRuleHit, check if rule.Sample is true; if so, determine the slot key using rule.SampleSlot ?? rule.Id (mirroring PowerShell lines 252-256), and set state.HitSample[slot] = entry.RawLine only if the slot is not already populated (first match wins). Ensure that when multiple rules share a SampleSlot (e.g., 'apogeeDrv.trend'), the first rule to fire captures the sample and subsequent rules reuse that slot without overwriting. Add accessor method GetRuleSample(AnalysisState state, string id) that looks up state.HitSample[id] or returns null if no sample was captured.
subtasks.testStrategy: Write unit tests that create rules with Sample=true and varying SampleSlot configurations: (1) rule with no SampleSlot uses Id as slot; (2) two rules sharing a SampleSlot capture only the first matching line; (3) processing multiple matches for a single rule does not overwrite the initial sample. Verify GetRuleSample returns the correct sample string or null for rules that have not fired.

subtasks.title: Implement FindingAt threshold evaluation and scoring logic
subtasks.description: Build the FindingAt threshold evaluation, rate calculation, severity weighting, and score computation logic that ranks detections by intensity (rate * severity weight) rather than volume, producing the 'over', 'rate', and 'score' fields used for sorting in Build-DetectionsObject equivalent C# payload builder.
subtasks.details: Implement logic that, for each rule with hits, computes: (1) 'over' = count / FindingAt if FindingAt > 0 else 0; (2) 'spanSec' = Max(RuleMinSpanSec=60, (lastTimestamp - firstTimestamp).TotalSeconds) using state.HitTime[ruleId].First and.Last; (3) 'rate' = count / spanSec * 3600.0 (hits per hour); (4) 'sevW' = weighted average of severities from state.HitSevs[ruleId] using RuleSevWeight map (FATAL=4.0, SEVERE=3.0, ERROR=2.0, WARNING=1.0, INFO=0.25); (5) 'score' = rate * sevW (mirroring PowerShell lines 404-437). Add constants: RuleMinSpanSec=60, RuleSevOrder=['FATAL','SEVERE','ERROR','WARNING','INFO'], RuleSevWeight as above. Store first/last timestamps in state.HitTime as DateTime values parsed from entry.Timestamp.
subtasks.testStrategy: Create unit tests that process LogEntry sequences with known timestamps and severities, then verify computed metrics: (1) a burst rule (e.g., 10 hits in 10 seconds) scores higher than sustained rule (10 hits in 10 minutes); (2) FATAL-severity rule scores higher than INFO-severity with same rate; (3) 'over' correctly reflects count/FindingAt ratio; (4) spanSec enforces 60-second minimum floor. Test edge cases like single-hit rules (spanSec=60) and rules with hits at identical timestamps.

subtasks.title: Enforce single-scope dev-gate mode
subtasks.description: Dev gate: Scope is a single string filter like Register-RuleSet; multi-scope/BACnet extras disabled until T8.
subtasks.details: Match Register-RuleSet (~194-205): if Scope set, require Comp.IndexOf(scope, OrdinalIgnoreCase) >= 0. Provide a gate flag/mode used by tests: DevGate (single-scope, no new BACnet-scoped families) vs ShipGate (T8). Do NOT stub or disable T5 hand-written analysis — it is required for byte-identical snapshots.
subtasks.testStrategy: Dev-gate fixtures: detection Ids/counts match 0.4.0. Enabling ship mode without T8 data should not silently change single-scope rules.

tasks.title: ReportWriter.cs and SnapshotBuilder.cs: HTML, text, and JSON renderers with parity gate
tasks.description: Implement snapshot building and report rendering for HTML, text, and JSON formats, achieving byte-identical outputs against 0.4.0 under the dev gate and providing an extensible foundation for later multi-scope and BACnet changes.
tasks.details:
SnapshotBuilder + ReportWriter: HTML/text/JSON matching 0.4.0 section structure. Dev gate (§9.2): byte-identical vs 0.4.0 aside from allowlist (meta.generated, tool/version banner, perf.health port/url, gen, documented formatting normals).
-Format Text|Html|Both; -OutPath; report exits with no port/browser; -NoPause semantics.
Build-Findings / detections ranking must use ported T5+T6 outputs.
