Use table-based assertions to confirm that section counts, headings, detection listings, and ranking orders match, documenting any expected differences once multi-scope and BACnet enhancements are later enabled. Add unit tests for SnapshotBuilder that validate construction of snapshot objects from synthetic AnalysisState and RuleEngine results, ensuring that nulls and empty collections are handled gracefully. For ReportWriter, create tests that confirm proper handling of -Format options, generation of files in expected locations under -OutPath, and correct exit codes in case of write failures. Additionally, verify JSON shape against the dashboard’s existing /api/snapshot contract so that HttpServer can rely on consistent snapshot structures.

subtasks.title: Design Snapshot class structure with Meta, Overview, Findings, Detections, and module sections
subtasks.description: Define the complete Snapshot type hierarchy mirroring PowerShell Build-SnapshotObject output, including MetaSection, OverviewSection, FindingSection, DetectionSection, DriverSection, ModuleSection, and PerformanceSection classes with all necessary properties for dashboard API compatibility and report rendering.
subtasks.details: Create a sealed Snapshot record with init-only properties for Meta (tool version, generated timestamp, author), Overview (total events, window span, severity distribution, area distribution, top-level metrics), Findings (IReadOnlyList<FindingSection> with Id, Group, Label, Scope, Hits, Measure, Samples, Threshold), Detections (pattern hits grouped by category), DriverSection (per-driver statistics and lifecycle events), ModuleSection (module load/unload tracking), and PerformanceSection (health status, startup time, performance categories). Ensure all types are serializable to JSON and match the shape expected by the existing ui\ dashboard code that consumes /api/snapshot. Reference Watch-PvssLog.ps1 lines 2757+ (Build-SnapshotObject) to understand the exact property names, nesting structure, and data types used in the PowerShell version. Document any intentional deviations from 0.4.0 schema.
subtasks.testStrategy: Create unit tests that instantiate Snapshot objects with representative data and serialize to JSON, comparing the resulting JSON shape against captured 0.4.0 /api/snapshot payloads to verify structural compatibility. Use JsonSerializer with consistent options (camelCase naming policy) and validate that all required fields are present and typed correctly for dashboard consumption.

subtasks.title: Implement SnapshotBuilder consuming AnalysisState and RuleEngine outputs
subtasks.description: Create SnapshotBuilder class that transforms AnalysisState aggregates and RuleEngine detection results into a fully populated Snapshot object, applying all business logic for metrics calculation, ranking, TopN selection, and sample formatting.
subtasks.details: Implement a SnapshotBuilder with a Build method that accepts AnalysisState (containing parsed events, per-minute buckets, module tracking, driver lifecycle, performance metrics) and RuleEngine results (pattern hits, bucket measures, findings, samples) and constructs the complete Snapshot hierarchy. Apply TopN ranking for patterns and modules using the same logic as PowerShell (sort by hit count descending, then lexicographically by pattern/module name). Format timestamps consistently using ISO 8601 or the exact format used in 0.4.0 reports. Populate Meta.Generated with current UTC timestamp, Meta.ToolVersion from VERSION.txt, and Meta.Author from configuration. Calculate Overview statistics by aggregating event counts across severity levels, areas, drivers, and time buckets. Transform RuleEngine FindingResult objects into FindingSection records with proper threshold formatting and sample truncation per SampleMaxChars configuration. Ensure SnapshotBuilder is stateless and can be called multiple times for dashboard refresh or different report configurations.
subtasks.testStrategy: Write integration tests that feed synthetic AnalysisState and RuleEngine results representing known scenarios (specific pattern counts, module sequences, findings above thresholds) and assert that the resulting Snapshot contains expected counts, rankings, and sections. Compare computed Overview metrics against hand-calculated values. Verify that TopN selection matches PowerShell behavior by running both engines on identical input and comparing ranked lists.

subtasks.title: Build HTML renderer matching 0.4.0 report structure, headings, tables, and styling
subtasks.description: Implement ReportWriter.WriteHtml method that generates HTML output byte-identical to 0.4.0 reports, preserving exact structure, CSS class names, table layouts, and heading hierarchy for dashboard and field continuity.
subtasks.details: Create WriteHtml method in ReportWriter that accepts a Snapshot and output path, emitting HTML markup matching the structure produced by Write-ReportSummary in Watch-PvssLog.ps1 line 5048+. Preserve DOCTYPE, meta tags, title format, inline CSS or stylesheet references, heading hierarchy (H1 for report title, H2 for sections like Overview, Findings, Detections, Modules), and table structures with correct column headers and data cell formatting. Use string interpolation or a lightweight templating approach (StringBuilder or StreamWriter with direct writes) rather than a heavy HTML generation library to maintain control over byte-exact output. Include all sections: Meta banner (tool version, generated timestamp), Overview summary table, Findings section with threshold-exceeded rules, Detections organized by Group/Label/Scope, per-Driver statistics, per-Module events, and Performance health summary. Apply CSS class names and IDs that the existing ui\ dashboard expects if HTML is served inline or if styling must match historical field reports. Handle -Organize switch (All, Severity, Driver) to adjust section grouping. Emit empty section placeholders or omit sections based on PowerShell precedent.
subtasks.testStrategy: Generate HTML reports from test Snapshots and compare against reference 0.4.0 HTML outputs using byte-identical diff (allowing only meta.generated timestamps and version banners per the allowlist). Validate that all required sections appear, tables are well-formed, and CSS class names match. Use an HTML validator to confirm markup correctness. Manually review rendered HTML in a browser to verify visual parity with 0.4.0 reports.

subtasks.title: Implement text format renderer for plain-text reports
subtasks.description: Create ReportWriter.WriteText method that produces plain-text report output matching the formatting, column alignment, and section structure of 0.4.0 text reports for command-line and log file compatibility.
subtasks.details: Implement WriteText method that renders Snapshot as formatted plain text with consistent column widths, heading underlines, and whitespace alignment matching PowerShell text output. Use fixed-width formatting or tab-delimited columns as appropriate for readability in console and text editors. Include all sections: Meta header (tool version, generated timestamp, author), Overview summary with labeled metrics, Findings list with rule ID/Group/Label/Scope/Hits/Measure/Threshold, Detections organized by category with pattern and hit count, per-Driver lifecycle and statistics, per-Module load/unload events, and Performance health. Apply text-mode line wrapping for long messages (sample lines) respecting SampleMaxChars. Ensure consistent line ending style (CRLF on Windows) and encoding (UTF-8 with BOM or ASCII) matching 0.4.0 convention. Handle -Organize switch to adjust section grouping in text as in HTML.
subtasks.testStrategy: Generate text reports from test Snapshots and compare against reference 0.4.0 text outputs using byte-identical diff (allowing only meta fields per allowlist). Verify that column alignment is consistent, headings are underlined correctly, and no extraneous whitespace or formatting differences exist. Test with wide and narrow terminal widths to confirm wrapping behavior if applicable. Validate UTF-8 encoding and line endings.

subtasks.title: Add JSON serializer producing dashboard-compatible snapshot payloads
subtasks.description: Implement ReportWriter.ToJson and WriteJson methods that serialize Snapshot to JSON in the exact schema expected by the dashboard /api/snapshot endpoint and batch report JSON output.
subtasks.details: Create ToJson method returning a JSON string and WriteJson method writing to a file path, both using System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer with options configured for camelCase property naming (or exact casing used by 0.4.0 /api/snapshot), indented formatting for report files, and any custom converters needed for enums or timestamps. Ensure the JSON schema matches the shape consumed by ui\ dashboard code: top-level 'meta', 'overview', 'findings', 'detections', 'drivers', 'modules', and 'performance' properties with nested objects and arrays matching PowerShell ConvertTo-Json output. Handle null or empty collections gracefully (emit empty arrays rather than null where expected by dashboard). Test round-trip serialization/deserialization to confirm schema stability. Use consistent timestamp formatting (ISO 8601 UTC) across all JSON fields.
subtasks.testStrategy: Serialize test Snapshots to JSON and compare against reference 0.4.0 /api/snapshot payloads and JSON report files using structural JSON diff (allowing only meta.generated and version fields per allowlist). Parse serialized JSON back into Snapshot objects to verify round-trip fidelity. Validate JSON syntax with a linter. Load JSON in the existing ui\ dashboard to confirm runtime compatibility and correct rendering of all sections.

subtasks.title: Integrate -Format switch handling for Text/Html/Both options
subtasks.description: Wire ReportWriter into the report-mode pipeline to honor the -Format CLI switch (Text, Html, Both), generating the appropriate output files with correct naming conventions and ensuring both formats are produced when -Format Both is specified.
subtasks.details: Extend Program.cs or Cli.cs report-mode execution path to call SnapshotBuilder.Build after rule application and then invoke ReportWriter.WriteHtml, WriteText, or both based on the -Format parameter value. When -Format is Text, generate only.txt output; when Html, generate only.html output; when Both (default), generate both.txt and.html files with consistent base names derived from -OutPath or default naming convention (e.g., 'PVSS_II_Report_<timestamp>.txt' and '.html'). Ensure JSON snapshot is also written if requested (implicit for dashboard mode /api/snapshot; explicit for batch report JSON output). Apply file path resolution and directory creation as needed. Emit console progress messages matching PowerShell verbosity ('Writing HTML report...', 'Writing text report...'). Respect -NoPause switch to skip the final 'Press any key to continue' prompt after report generation.
subtasks.testStrategy: Run report mode with each -Format option (Text, Html, Both) and verify that the expected output files are created with correct extensions and content. Test -OutPath with explicit file paths, directory paths, and default (current directory) to confirm naming and placement logic. Verify that -NoPause suppresses the pause prompt. Compare file timestamps and sizes against expectations. Run end-to-end tests on representative log files and validate that all three formats are generated correctly when -Format Both is used.

subtasks.title: Implement -OutPath and -NoPause semantics
subtasks.description: Ensure report-mode output respects the -OutPath parameter for custom file placement and directory creation, and that -NoPause correctly suppresses the post-report pause prompt in batch scenarios.
subtasks.details: Implement -OutPath logic in Program.cs or ReportWriter to accept either a directory path (generate default-named files in that directory) or a full file path with base name (append.txt/.html extensions as appropriate). Create the target directory if it does not exist, with error handling for permission issues or invalid paths. Resolve relative paths against the current working directory. Apply the same auto-naming convention used in PowerShell (include timestamp or log file name in generated report names). Implement -NoPause by conditionally skipping Console.ReadKey() or equivalent pause after report generation completes; ensure pause is shown by default in interactive scenarios (to allow user review of console output) but suppressed when -NoPause is specified or when running in non-interactive contexts (redirected stdin). Emit a final console message indicating the output path(s) of generated reports for user confirmation.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test -OutPath with various input patterns: directory only, full file path, relative path, absolute path, non-existent directory (confirm auto-creation), invalid path (confirm error message). Verify that generated files appear at the specified location with correct names. Test -NoPause in both interactive console and batch script contexts (simulated non-interactive stdin) to confirm the pause is correctly suppressed. Check console output for file path confirmation messages.

subtasks.title: Establish parity testing infrastructure with byte-identical comparison and allowlist
subtasks.description: Create automated parity tests that compare C# pipeline outputs (HTML, text, JSON) against reference 0.4.0 PowerShell outputs on a fixed corpus, using a diff allowlist for tolerated meta field differences and failing on unexpected discrepancies.
subtasks.details: Harness: PS 0.4.0 -Report vs C# -Report on curated fixtures (include CNS/Apogee/BACnet sections). Diff HTML/text byte-identical with allowlist; JSON structural compare. Fail on unexpected diffs. Do not implement startup-plume tagging (non-goal); fixtures may contain plume-like lines as ordinary input.
subtasks.testStrategy: Execute the parity test suite on the fixed corpus and confirm that all tests pass under dev gate configuration (single-scope rules only). Manually review diff reports for any allowlisted differences to verify they are legitimate (timestamps, version strings). Introduce intentional regressions (e.g., change a section heading, alter a metric calculation) and confirm that parity tests fail as expected with clear error messages. Document the allowlist rules and test corpus in project documentation for maintainability.

tasks.title: Enable §2.1 exceptions: multi-scope rules, BACnet-scoped families, verify manager ranges
tasks.description: Extend the rule system and CLI to support multi-scope rules and BACnet-specific families while enabling interactive manager pick range syntax, documenting expected report deltas versus 0.4.0 at the ship gate.
tasks.details:
Enable §2.1 exceptions AFTER T7 dev gate is green:
1) Multi-scope: Scope as string or list; dual-driver rules without breaking single-scope rows.
2) BACnet-scoped rule families: add BACnet-scoped counterparts for the Apogee-shaped ApogeeDrv families (PRD: four Apogee-shaped families — mirror ApogeeDrv detection families under BACnet scopes; do NOT widen existing Apogee Scope values). Derive from existing apogeeDrv.* rules + T1 inventory — do not invent unrelated detections.
3) Manager ranges: already implemented in T3.5 — verify wired for -Interactive; fix gaps only.
Record expected snapshot deltas in PROGRESS-V0.5.md. Ship gate: fail only on unexpected diffs.
tasks.testStrategy: Create targeted tests for multi-scope rules that feed synthetic logs representing dual-driver scenarios, verifying that rules operate across all configured scopes and produce combined detections without double-counting or scope leakage. For BACnet-scoped rules, use fixtures containing BACnet-specific traces and Apogee traces, asserting that new rules fire only under BACnet scopes and that existing Apogee behaviors remain unchanged. Adjust regression tests from the dev gate to produce updated expectations under the ship gate, documenting expected differences in PROGRESS-V0.5 and ensuring that any unexpected divergence triggers test failures. For manager range prompts, introduce unit tests that parse inputs such as "1", "2-4", and "1-3,10" and confirm that the resulting selection lists are correct and stable, and run interactive integration tests to ensure that prompts and confirmations behave as described. Finally, re-run full pipeline tests with the §2.1 exceptions enabled, confirming that snapshot outputs align with updated expectations and that CLI behavior still matches operator workflows.

subtasks.title: Augment RuleDefinition to support multi-scope as string or list
subtasks.description: Modify RuleDefinition record to allow Scope field to accept either a single string or IReadOnlyList of strings for multi-scope rule support.
subtasks.details: Update the RuleDefinition sealed record to change the Scope property from a single string to support both string and IReadOnlyList of string types. Implement proper type handling so existing single-scope rules continue to work without modification while new multi-scope rules can specify multiple scopes as a list.
subtasks.testStrategy: Create unit tests that instantiate RuleDefinition with both single-scope string and multi-scope list inputs, verifying that both formats are accepted and properly stored.

subtasks.title: Update RuleEngine to evaluate multi-scope rules across all configured scopes
subtasks.description: Extend RuleEngine logic to iterate over all scopes defined in multi-scope rules, ensuring rules evaluate correctly across dual-driver scenarios without double-counting.
subtasks.details: Modify the RuleEngine evaluation logic to check if a rule has multiple scopes and iterate through each scope during rule matching. Implement safeguards to prevent double-counting when a log entry matches multiple scopes within the same rule.
subtasks.testStrategy: Develop targeted tests using synthetic logs representing dual-driver scenarios with entries that fall under multiple scopes. Verify that multi-scope rules trigger correctly for each applicable scope without double-counting.

subtasks.title: Implement BACnet-scoped rule families for four Apogee-shaped drivers
subtasks.description: Create BACnet-specific rule definitions for the four Apogee-shaped drivers without widening existing Apogee scopes, ensuring clear tagging and accounting in detection counts.
subtasks.details: Add BACnet-scoped families mirroring ApogeeDrv-shaped rules (trend/alert/query/getData-style families per PRD §2.1). Keep Apogee Scope values unchanged. Tag Ids/groups so ship-gate diffs are documentable. Use existing Apogee rule patterns as templates; confirm exact Id list during implementation against inventory — do not open-ended "research" new product behavior.
subtasks.testStrategy: Use test fixtures containing BACnet-specific log patterns that match the four driver families. Verify that BACnet rules trigger only on BACnet-scoped entries and not on Apogee entries, confirming scope isolation.

subtasks.title: Add configuration toggles for dev-gate vs ship-gate behavior separation
subtasks.description: Introduce build-time constants or configuration toggles that control whether multi-scope and BACnet rules are active, enabling dev-gate parity validation before ship-gate enhancements.
subtasks.details: Create a configuration mechanism that separates dev-gate behavior (single-scope only, no BACnet extras) from ship-gate behavior (multi-scope and BACnet rules active). Implement a GateMode or similar setting that can be toggled to switch between modes.
subtasks.testStrategy: Run the analyzer in dev-gate mode against the 50 MB corpus and compare output byte-for-byte with 0.4.0 baseline to verify parity. Then switch to ship-gate mode and verify that multi-scope and BACnet rules become active.

subtasks.title: Verify interactive manager range parsing (owned by T3.5)
subtasks.description: Confirm 1-3,10 works end-to-end in -Interactive; fill any gaps only.
subtasks.details: T3.5 owns ParseManagerRange. Here: integration check with interactive prompt flow and ship-gate acceptance item 10. Fix only if incomplete.
subtasks.testStrategy: Interactive/integration tests for 1, 2-4, 1-3,10 and invalid input.

subtasks.title: Document expected report deltas in PROGRESS-V0.5 for multi-scope and BACnet
subtasks.description: Create comprehensive documentation in PROGRESS-V0.5.md recording the known differences in detection counts and report sections introduced by multi-scope rules and BACnet-scoped rule families versus 0.4.0.
subtasks.details: Create or update PROGRESS-V0.5.md to include a dedicated section documenting expected report deltas versus the 0.4.0 baseline. For each multi-scope rule and BACnet rule family introduced, document the specific detection count changes, new report sections, and scope-specific findings.
subtasks.testStrategy: Review the documentation against actual test runs in both dev-gate and ship-gate modes to verify that all documented deltas are accurate and complete. Ensure that any unexpected differences between documented and actual output are investigated.

subtasks.title: Adjust ship-gate tests to expect documented deltas and fail on unexpected differences
subtasks.description: Update ship-gate test expectations to treat documented detection count and section differences as passing while maintaining failure detection for any unexpected deviations from expected behavior.
subtasks.details: Modify the ship-gate test suite to incorporate the documented deltas from PROGRESS-V0.5 as expected outcomes. Implement test assertions that verify the specific multi-scope and BACnet detection counts and section additions documented in subtask 6 are present in ship-gate output.
subtasks.testStrategy: Run the complete ship-gate test suite against the 50 MB corpus and verify that all tests pass with the section 2.1 enhancements active. Introduce intentional deviations and confirm that tests correctly fail.

tasks.title: HttpServer.cs: 127.0.0.1 listener, static ui\, and inventory /api/* routes
tasks.description: Implement an embedded HTTP server bound to 127.0.0.1 that serves static ui assets and exposes all required /api/* routes for the dashboard, following the API inventory defined in phase 5A.
tasks.details:
HttpServer on 127.0.0.1 only (preferred port + MaxPortTries fallback). Serve Watch\ui\ statically. Implement ALL routes from the T1.1 inventory — at minimum:
- GET /api/health
- GET /api/pulse
- GET /api/section
- GET /api/manager
- GET /api/snapshot
- POST /api/control (JSON body.action = pause|resume|restart|setWindow|note — mirror PS switch)
- POST /api/logPath
Do NOT invent /api/start, /api/pause, /api/resume, /api/restart as separate paths. JSON keys/types must match what ui\ already calls.
tasks.testStrategy: Contract tests vs 0.4.0 JSON shapes on fixtures. Static ui loads. Bind address is 127.0.0.1 only. Control actions via /api/control.

subtasks.title: Design HttpServer class with HttpListener and port binding logic
subtasks.description: Create the HttpServer.cs class using HttpListener bound to 127.0.0.1 with configurable port, implementing fallback port tries and clean lifecycle management.
subtasks.details: Implement HttpServer class using System.Net.HttpListener to bind exclusively to 127.0.0.1 (localhost) with a configurable port from watch-config.txt. Add port fallback logic that tries MaxPortTries sequential ports if the preferred port is unavailable, mirroring PowerShell behavior. Implement Start(prefix), Stop(), and Dispose() methods with proper lifecycle management. Include async ListenLoop() that calls GetContextAsync() to handle incoming requests. Add thread-safe state tracking for IsRunning and BoundPort properties. Ensure the server binds only to localhost and never exposes external network surfaces, satisfying the security requirement. Include proper exception handling for port binding failures and graceful shutdown semantics.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests verify HttpServer can start on specified port, fallback to next port when unavailable, and bind only to 127.0.0.1. Integration tests confirm lifecycle methods (Start/Stop/Dispose) work correctly and that external network access is blocked.

subtasks.title: Implement static file serving from Watch/ui/ directory
subtasks.description: Add static file serving functionality to HttpServer that maps URL paths to files under ui/ directory with content-type detection and 404 handling.
subtasks.details: Implement ServeStaticFile() method that maps HTTP request paths to physical files under Watch/ui/ directory. Add content-type detection based on file extension (.html -> text/html; charset=utf-8,.css -> text/css; charset=utf-8,.js -> application/javascript; charset=utf-8,.svg -> image/svg+xml,.png -> image/png, etc.). Handle missing files with proper 404 responses including appropriate status codes and error messages. Implement path traversal protection to prevent access outside ui/ directory. Set appropriate response headers including Content-Type with charset, Content-Length, and Cache-Control. Support index.html as default document for root path requests. Use async file I/O with proper stream handling and disposal.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit tests verify content-type headers are correct for each file type (.html,.css,.js,.svg). Integration tests confirm 404 responses for missing files, path traversal attempts are blocked, and index.html is served for root path. Performance tests ensure async file I/O handles concurrent requests.

subtasks.title: Consume T1.1 API inventory (do not rediscover from scratch)
subtasks.description: Checklist for implementation: every route/method/schema from the 5A inventory.
subtasks.details: Use T1.1 document as the definition of done for T9. Expand any gaps by re-reading Watch-PvssLog.ps1 handlers (~4458+). Must include /api/control actions and /api/logPath. Explicitly reject inventing alternate control URLs.
subtasks.testStrategy: Checklist checked off against PS handlers 1:1.

subtasks.title: Implement /api/health and /api/pulse endpoints with JSON responses
subtasks.description: Develop /api/health and /api/pulse endpoints that return JSON responses matching the existing PowerShell API contract and dashboard expectations.
subtasks.details: Implement GET /api/health and GET /api/pulse with the same fields the dashboard expects (generation, loading, loadProgressPct, paused, findings, series, etc. per inventory).
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit/integration: JSON field names match 0.4.0 / T1.1 inventory; query params and defaults match PS; sinceGeneration behavior preserved.

subtasks.title: Add /api/section and /api/manager data endpoints backed by SnapshotBuilder
subtasks.description: Implement section and manager detail endpoints that query SnapshotBuilder and AnalysisState to return filtered detection data for specific rule groups and manager components.
subtasks.details: Implement /api/section endpoint (GET) that requires 'name' query parameter (e.g., 'bacnet', 'cns', 'apogee') and optional severities/areas filters, returning JSON with section name, window descriptor, detections array (each with id, group, label, hits, measure, buckets, samples, finding), and aggregated metrics. Implement /api/manager endpoint (GET) that requires 'name' query parameter (manager component name) and filters, returning JSON with manager name, window descriptor, log line count, severity distribution, timeline series, and sample log lines. Integrate with SnapshotBuilder to access aggregated detection state and use RuleEngine results to populate responses. Apply severity and area filters to returned data. Handle unknown section/manager names with 400 Bad Request responses. Ensure JSON keys and structure match 0.4.0 PowerShell output exactly so dashboard renders correctly without modification.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration vs PS responses for /api/section and /api/manager on fixtures; missing name → same error behavior as 0.4.0.

subtasks.title: Implement /api/snapshot endpoint returning full snapshot JSON
subtasks.description: Create /api/snapshot endpoint that serializes complete AnalysisState and SnapshotBuilder data into full snapshot JSON matching the report structure expected by the dashboard.
subtasks.details: Implement /api/snapshot endpoint (GET) that returns comprehensive JSON snapshot including all fields from /api/pulse plus complete detections data for all sections, full manager list with health metrics (starts, stops, restarts, blocking, unblocked), detailed projectLifecycle with cycles array, hourly aggregations, and all samples. Serialize using SnapshotBuilder.BuildSnapshot() method to gather data from AnalysisState, ensuring consistency with batch report output format. Include metadata like generation timestamp, version, author, and window configuration. Ensure response size is manageable (apply capping limits as in PowerShell: 200 project events, samples per pattern limit). Set proper Content-Type and consider Content-Encoding: gzip for large responses. Handle case where no log session is active (return 400 with appropriate error message).
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration: /api/snapshot shape matches report/dashboard contract from T1.1; caps (e.g. 200 project events) preserved.

subtasks.title: Implement POST /api/control and POST /api/logPath
subtasks.description: Port control plane from PowerShell — single control endpoint + logPath POST.
subtasks.details: POST /api/control: parse JSON action; implement pause, resume, restart (config reload + reset analysis), setWindow, note, matching the PS switch. POST /api/logPath: validate path, open log, update LogPath write-back rules (dashboard only). Match status codes and response bodies from 0.4.0.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration: pause/resume/restart/setWindow/note via /api/control; logPath via /api/logPath; unknown action errors like PS.

subtasks.title: Integrate HttpServer with Program.cs for dashboard mode and ensure security
subtasks.description: Wire HttpServer into Program.cs dashboard mode pipeline, implement request routing, ensure localhost-only binding, and add comprehensive error handling and logging.
subtasks.details: Dashboard mode starts HttpServer after CLI parse; serve ui\; localhost only; clean shutdown. Report mode must not start the listener.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration tests verify dashboard mode starts HttpServer on configured port, serves both static files and API endpoints, and shuts down cleanly on exit. Security tests confirm external network access is blocked and only 127.0.0.1 bindings work. Test port fallback logic when preferred port is unavailable. Verify error handling for malformed requests, missing files, and server errors returns appropriate status codes. Load tests confirm concurrent request handling works correctly.

tasks.title: Dashboard catch-up, tailing, restart behavior, and config reload integration
tasks.description: Integrate log catch-up and tailing behavior with the dashboard’s HttpServer, implementing progress percentage, restart semantics, and configuration reload so that UI workflows mirror 0.4.0.
tasks.details: Integrate T4 catch-up/tail with HttpServer: progress % on pulse/health; transition to tail; restart via POST /api/control action=restart reloads config (T2.6) and reinits state; Start/logPath write-back per T2.5; window changes via control setWindow without reinventing Entire-cache (deferred). Concurrency: safe snapshots for HTTP readers. Cleanup on repeated restarts.
tasks.testStrategy: Develop integration tests that run the dashboard pipeline on a fixed log fixture, exercising catch-up and tail phases and verifying that progress percentages move from 0 to 100 during catch-up and stabilize in tailing while new lines are appended. For restart tests, simulate a configuration change by editing watch-config.txt during runtime, trigger a restart via an API call, and confirm that the analyzer reloads configuration, adjusts its behavior accordingly, and resumes analysis without leaving HttpServer in an inconsistent state. Validate that LogPath is written back to watch-config.txt when the dashboard selects a new log and that report mode does not write LogPath. Additionally, verify that repeated restarts do not leak resources or leave orphaned tail loops, and ensure that snapshot data presented via APIs accurately reflects the state of analysis both during catch-up and tailing. Finally, compare dashboard behavior against 0.4.0’s workflows, noting any intentional differences only where §2.1 enhancements apply.

subtasks.title: Implement catch-up phase with progress percentage tracking
subtasks.description: Build the initial catch-up phase that parses PVSS_II.log from start (or selected window start) to current EOF, tracking file position versus total size to compute and expose progress percentages.
subtasks.details: Wire T4 catch-up progress into dashboard Sync-equivalent state (loadProgressPct/loadMessage). Do not reimplement the file loop from scratch.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test CatchUpAsync with a fixed 1MB log fixture, verifying progress moves from 0% to 100% as bytes are consumed. Integration test with ~10MB corpus ensuring window selections start at correct file positions and progress calculations are accurate within 1%.

subtasks.title: Expose catch-up progress via /api/health or /api/pulse endpoints
subtasks.description: Integrate catch-up progress percentage into the HttpServer API so the dashboard UI can display real-time progress during the initial log scan.
subtasks.details: Add a progress field to the /api/health or /api/pulse response that returns the current catch-up percentage (0-100) and a phase indicator (e.g., 'catching-up' vs 'tailing'). Ensure the HttpServer can safely read the progress value from LogParser without blocking the analysis thread. Consider using a thread-safe property or concurrent data structure. The dashboard expects to poll this endpoint every 1-2 seconds during catch-up, so ensure the response is lightweight and does not interfere with log parsing performance.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration test launching dashboard mode with a 5MB log, polling /api/pulse every 500ms, and verifying that progress values are monotonically increasing from 0 to 100 and that the phase transitions from 'catching-up' to 'tailing' once catch-up completes.

subtasks.title: Build seamless transition from catch-up to tailing loop
subtasks.description: Implement the transition from catch-up mode to continuous tailing mode, where the analyzer monitors the log file for new appended lines and processes them in real-time.
subtasks.details: After CatchUpAsync reaches EOF, transition into TailAsync mode that continuously monitors the log file for new bytes. Use a polling loop (e.g., check every 500ms-1s) or FileSystemWatcher to detect new content. When new lines are available, read and process them through RuleEngine and update AnalysisState incrementally. Ensure no lines are lost during the catch-up-to-tail transition by remembering the file position. Handle log rotation scenarios gracefully (file shrinks, gets replaced). Keep the tail loop responsive to cancellation tokens for clean shutdown and restart behavior. Ensure state updates during tailing are consistent with catch-up phase behavior.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration test that runs catch-up on a 1MB log, transitions to tail mode, then appends 100 new lines to the log file and verifies all 100 lines are detected and processed within 2 seconds. Verify no duplicate or missed lines at the transition boundary.

subtasks.title: Add periodic pulse updates during tailing for live dashboard refresh
subtasks.description: Implement periodic emission of pulse updates via /api/pulse during the tailing phase so the dashboard UI can reflect live detections, updated metrics, and new snapshots without requiring page reloads.
subtasks.details: During TailAsync, after processing each batch of new lines (or on a timer every 2-5 seconds), trigger an internal pulse event that updates the snapshot available to /api/pulse and /api/snapshot. Ensure SnapshotBuilder is invoked to reflect the latest AnalysisState and RuleEngine results. The pulse response should include updated detection counts, top patterns, severity distributions, and other dashboard-critical metrics. Coordinate timing to balance responsiveness (dashboard sees updates quickly) versus overhead (don't rebuild snapshots too frequently). Ensure thread-safe access to snapshots so HTTP handlers never see partial or inconsistent state.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration test that runs tail mode while appending batches of 20 lines every 3 seconds to the log, polling /api/pulse every 2 seconds, and verifying that detection counts and pattern lists are updated within one poll cycle after each batch is written.

subtasks.title: Implement restart semantics with watch-config.txt reload and state reinitialization
subtasks.description: Build restart logic that allows the dashboard to trigger a full re-analysis: reload watch-config.txt, apply new configuration values, reset AnalysisState, and re-run catch-up and tail without unbinding HttpServer.
subtasks.details: restart action: stop catch-up/tail, reset analysis, Apply-WatchConfig -Runtime equivalent, idle until new Start/logPath — match PS restart block.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration test that starts dashboard mode, modifies watch-config.txt to change window from Entire to LastHours=2, triggers restart via API, and verifies that the new analysis reflects only the last 2 hours of log data. Confirm HttpServer remains responsive and bound to the same port throughout.

subtasks.title: Ensure LogPath write-back to config on dashboard Start, prevent in report mode
subtasks.description: Implement the rule that dashboard mode writes the user-selected LogPath back to watch-config.txt when the Start action is triggered, while report mode never modifies the config file.
subtasks.details: Ensure dashboard log open / POST /api/logPath persists LogPath; report mode never does. Owned by T2.5 — verify integration only.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test for Config.WriteLogPath that modifies a temp watch-config.txt, verifies LogPath line is updated while other keys remain unchanged. Integration test for dashboard Start action that selects a new LogPath, starts analysis, and confirms watch-config.txt reflects the new path. Report mode test verifying config file is never modified even with -LogPath override.

subtasks.title: Coordinate concurrency between log reading, state updates, and HTTP handlers
subtasks.description: Implement thread-safe coordination so that log parsing/tailing, AnalysisState updates, snapshot generation, and HTTP request handling do not produce race conditions or inconsistent views.
subtasks.details: Use appropriate concurrency primitives (locks, ReaderWriterLockSlim, ConcurrentCollections, or immutable snapshots) to ensure that: (1) AnalysisState is not modified while SnapshotBuilder reads it; (2) HTTP handlers serving /api/pulse and /api/snapshot see a consistent snapshot even if new lines are being processed concurrently; (3) restart operations cleanly cancel and replace the tail loop without leaving orphaned threads or partial state. Prefer lock-free approaches where possible (e.g., atomic snapshot swaps) to minimize blocking. Document concurrency model in comments. Ensure that high-frequency tailing updates do not starve HTTP request threads or vice versa.
subtasks.testStrategy: Concurrency stress test that runs tail mode while simultaneously hammering /api/pulse with 10 concurrent requests per second for 30 seconds, verifying no deadlocks, crashes, or inconsistent snapshot data (e.g., detection counts that don't match pattern lists). Unit tests for snapshot swap atomicity.

subtasks.title: Handle window selection changes and re-analysis without restarting HttpServer
subtasks.description: Support dynamic window changes (e.g., switching from Entire to LastHours=4) via the dashboard UI, re-running analysis without tearing down and rebinding HttpServer.
subtasks.details: Extend restart logic to allow window parameter updates via the dashboard. When the user changes window selection (Entire, relative, or absolute From/To), treat it as a restart trigger: cancel current tail, reload config or accept UI-provided window params, reset AnalysisState, re-run catch-up with new window, transition to tailing. Ensure HttpServer port binding remains unchanged. Provide feedback to the UI during the re-analysis phase (progress percentage, phase indicator). Validate that window changes apply immediately and that stale data from the old window is fully cleared from snapshots.
subtasks.testStrategy: Integration test that starts dashboard in Entire mode, switches to LastHours=1 via UI, and verifies that the snapshot reflects only the last hour of data within 5 seconds. Confirm HttpServer remains on the same port and that progress percentage restarts from 0% during re-analysis.

subtasks.title: Validate resource cleanup and prevent leaked tail loops on repeated restarts
subtasks.description: Ensure that repeated restart cycles cleanly dispose of file handles, cancel tail loops, release snapshots, and do not leak memory or threads over the lifetime of the dashboard session.
subtasks.details: Implement proper IDisposable patterns for LogParser, FileStreams, and any other resources. Ensure CancellationTokenSource is created fresh for each restart and that old tokens are disposed. Verify that FileStream handles to PVSS_II.log are closed before reopening on restart. Use weak references or periodic GC monitoring in tests to detect memory leaks. Ensure that repeated restart cycles (e.g., 50 restarts in a row) do not increase memory usage, thread count, or leave orphaned tail loops running. Profile with a memory/thread monitoring tool during multi-restart scenarios.
subtasks.testStrategy: Stress test that triggers 50 consecutive restarts via /api/restart, monitoring process memory, handle count, and thread count. Verify metrics remain stable (within 10% variance) across all restarts. Unit tests for Dispose patterns ensuring FileStreams and CancellationTokenSources are released. Check that no ObjectDisposedException is thrown during or after restart cycles.

tasks.title: Build, publish, launcher integration, and field package layout for 0.5.0
tasks.description: Configure build and publish processes, update launchers to call DesigoLogWatcher.exe, and finalize the field package layout so that operators can use the C# runtime with unchanged workflows and without requiring PowerShell or a global.NET install.
tasks.details: Field package 0.5.0: publish single-file exe into Watch\; copy/keep ui\, watch-config.txt, VERSION.txt=0.5.0; update Run-Watch.cmd / Run-Report*.cmd to call Watch\DesigoLogWatcher.exe with same arg forwarding; remove Watch-PvssLog.ps1 from field zip (keep in repo for parity oracle); update readMe/CHANGELOG for operators ("faster engine; same usage" + §2.1 notes). csproj publish flags should already exist from T1 — this task finishes packaging/docs/launcher cutover and smoke.
tasks.testStrategy: Perform end-to-end tests by building and publishing the project, constructing a field zip, and deploying it to a clean Windows machine that lacks both PowerShell and a pre-installed.NET runtime to confirm that the single-file self-contained executable runs successfully. Invoke dashboard and report modes via the updated launchers, verifying that CLI arguments and interactive prompts behave exactly as before, that logs are discovered and opened correctly, and that report outputs are written to expected locations. Validate that the package layout matches the PRD’s diagram, that VERSION.txt reports 0.5.0, and that readMe.txt and CHANGELOG.txt accurately describe the runtime change and §2.1 detection upgrades. Additionally, run basic smoke tests across different Windows versions in the supported OS matrix to confirm compatibility with net10.0-windows and that no unexpected dependencies are introduced.

subtasks.title: Configure DesigoLogWatcher.csproj for single-file self-contained deployment
subtasks.description: Set up the.csproj file with all required properties for producing a self-contained, single-file Windows executable that bundles the.NET runtime and native libraries.
subtasks.details: Confirm csproj still matches PRD §6.1 (from T1). Adjust only if publish smoke finds gaps (native libs, single-file).
subtasks.testStrategy: Build the project using 'dotnet build src\DesigoLogWatcher\DesigoLogWatcher.csproj -c Release' and verify successful compilation. Then publish using 'dotnet publish src\DesigoLogWatcher\DesigoLogWatcher.csproj -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained' to confirm a single executable is produced with all dependencies bundled.

subtasks.title: Configure dotnet publish command and Watch/ output directory structure
subtasks.description: Establish the publish workflow that outputs DesigoLogWatcher.exe and required assets to the Watch/ directory, ensuring ui/ assets are included and the directory structure matches field deployment requirements.
subtasks.details: Document/script: dotnet publish... -o Watch\ and ensure ui\ lands beside exe (content copy or existing folder). Field zip excludes src\, docs\,.git,.taskmaster.
subtasks.testStrategy: Execute 'dotnet publish src\DesigoLogWatcher\DesigoLogWatcher.csproj -c Release -o Watch\' and inspect the Watch/ directory to confirm DesigoLogWatcher.exe is present, ui/ folder contains dashboard assets, and watch-config.txt exists. Run DesigoLogWatcher.exe manually to verify it launches without errors.

subtasks.title: Update launcher batch scripts to invoke DesigoLogWatcher.exe with argument forwarding
subtasks.description: Modify Run-Watch.cmd, Run-Report.cmd, and Run-Report-Interactive.cmd to call Watch\DesigoLogWatcher.exe instead of powershell.exe, preserving all CLI argument forwarding and usage semantics.
subtasks.details: Edit Run-Watch.cmd, Run-Report.cmd, and Run-Report-Interactive.cmd to replace the existing 'powershell.exe -File Watch-PvssLog.ps1' invocations with 'Watch\DesigoLogWatcher.exe %*' to forward all command-line arguments. Ensure the batch script structure remains simple and readable, using a pattern like: @echo off\nset EXE=Watch\DesigoLogWatcher.exe\n"%EXE%" %*. Verify that all existing CLI flags (e.g., --window, --port, --log-path) continue to work identically to the PowerShell implementation. Preserve any environment variable settings or error handling present in the original scripts.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test each launcher script by invoking it with various argument combinations (e.g., 'Run-Watch.cmd --window Today', 'Run-Report.cmd --window Week') and confirm that DesigoLogWatcher.exe receives and processes the arguments correctly. Compare output and behavior against documented 0.4.x workflows to ensure parity.

subtasks.title: Update VERSION.txt to 0.5.0 and revise documentation for runtime transition
subtasks.description: Set VERSION.txt to 0.5.0 and update readMe.txt and CHANGELOG.txt to document the PowerShell-to-C# runtime transition, emphasizing performance improvements and unchanged operator workflows.
subtasks.details: Edit VERSION.txt to set the version string to '0.5.0'. Update readMe.txt to explain that v0.5.0 replaces the PowerShell engine with a self-contained C# runtime (DesigoLogWatcher.exe) that no longer requires PowerShell or a separate.NET installation, while maintaining identical CLI usage and dashboard functionality. Highlight performance improvements (e.g., faster parsing and analysis compared to ~8-minute PowerShell baseline). Update CHANGELOG.txt with a v0.5.0 section detailing: runtime engine change, performance enhancements, removal of PowerShell dependency, and confirmation that all existing watch-config.txt settings and launcher workflows remain compatible. Ensure documentation is operator-friendly and emphasizes continuity.
subtasks.testStrategy: Review updated readMe.txt and CHANGELOG.txt for clarity, completeness, and accuracy. Verify VERSION.txt reads '0.5.0'. Have a second reviewer or operator persona read the documentation to confirm it clearly communicates the changes without causing confusion about usage.

subtasks.title: Assemble field deployment zip package with correct inclusions and exclusions
subtasks.description: Create the field-ready zip package containing Watch/, launchers, VERSION.txt, readMe.txt, CHANGELOG.txt, and watch-config.txt, while excluding src/, docs/, and development-only files.
subtasks.details: Construct a zip archive for field deployment named 'PVSII_Log_v0.5.0.zip' (or similar) that includes: Watch/ folder with DesigoLogWatcher.exe and ui/ assets, VERSION.txt, watch-config.txt, readMe.txt, CHANGELOG.txt, and the three launcher batch scripts (Run-Watch.cmd, Run-Report.cmd, Run-Report-Interactive.cmd) in the root. Explicitly exclude the src/ directory, docs/ directory,.git/,.taskmaster/, and any other development or internal files. Verify the archive structure matches the PRD's prescribed field layout so operators receive only runtime and usage files. Document the packaging procedure (manual or scripted) for repeatable builds.
subtasks.testStrategy: Extract the zip archive to a temporary directory and verify the contents match expected inclusions (Watch/DesigoLogWatcher.exe, ui/, launchers, docs) and exclusions (no src/, no.git/). Confirm the directory structure is clean and operator-ready.

subtasks.title: Validate deployment on clean Windows machine without.NET runtime or PowerShell
subtasks.description: Perform end-to-end acceptance testing by deploying the field zip to a fresh Windows system that lacks PowerShell and.NET runtime, confirming the self-contained executable runs successfully for dashboard and report modes.
subtasks.details: Extract the field zip package (created in subtask 5) onto a clean Windows machine (physical or VM) that does not have PowerShell available and does not have a.NET runtime pre-installed. Execute Run-Watch.cmd to launch dashboard mode and verify the dashboard UI is accessible via browser at the configured port. Execute Run-Report.cmd to generate a static HTML report and confirm the report is written successfully. Test CLI argument forwarding by running launchers with various flags (e.g., --window, --log-path). Verify that DesigoLogWatcher.exe operates without errors, dependencies are fully bundled, and operator workflows are identical to 0.4.x. Document any issues encountered and confirm resolution before release.
subtasks.testStrategy: On a clean Windows test environment, run all three launcher scripts with representative arguments and log fixtures. Verify dashboard startup, /api/pulse endpoint, report generation, and HTML output quality. Confirm no missing DLL errors, no PowerShell not found errors, and no.NET runtime missing errors. Compare behavior and output against 0.4.0 baseline to ensure parity and performance improvements.

tasks.title: Performance measurement, parity verification, and optional Entire-window cache decision
tasks.description: Measure performance on the ~50 MB corpus, verify parity against 0.4.0 under dev and ship gates, and decide whether to implement an Entire-window cache for dashboard mode based on real cold-parse numbers.
tasks.details: Measure ~50MB corpus timings (aspiration <5s / stretch <1s — not hard fail). Dev-gate parity already from T7; reconfirm. Ship-gate: §2.1 deltas documented in PROGRESS (T8) — fail unexpected only. API contract checks. Acceptance checklist §11. Optional Entire-window cache ONLY if cold Entire parse is still multi-second per §4.6 (serve results first, then cache). Write PROGRESS-V0.5.md.
tasks.testStrategy: Execute performance tests on representative hardware and the ~50 MB PVSS_II.log corpus, capturing timing metrics for report-mode entire-file scan plus HTML write and dashboard cold Entire parse, and compare these against the 0.4.0 PowerShell baseline, confirming that any substantial reduction constitutes a successful rewrite even without meeting stretch goals. Perform dev-gate parity tests by running both 0.4.0 and the C# analyzer with single-scope rules on static logs, diffing HTML, text, and JSON outputs and allowing only predefined meta differences; any unexpected mismatch should fail tests and prompt investigation. After enabling multi-scope and BACnet rules, update expectations to treat known deltas as successes and continue failing on unanticipated differences, ensuring that rule Ids still fire and counts align with the documented exceptions. Verify dashboard API contracts by comparing JSON schemas for pulse, section, manager, and health endpoints against 0.4.0 responses on fixtures, and confirm that config behavior and launcher usage meet all acceptance checklist items. Finally, if an Entire-window cache is implemented, add tests that validate cache correctness, invalidation triggers, and user experience, confirming that results are served before caching and that any caching progress indicators behave as expected.

subtasks.title: Establish performance test harness for ~50MB PVSS_II.log corpus
subtasks.description: Create a dedicated performance testing harness that measures entire-file scan and HTML write times for the ~50MB PVSS_II.log corpus, providing instrumentation hooks for timing critical operations in both report and dashboard modes.
subtasks.details: Implement a PerfMetrics class with properties for ReportEntireDuration, DashboardColdEntireDuration, ScanDuration, HTMLWriteDuration, and other key metrics. Create a performance test runner that loads the static PVSS_II.log corpus from docs/PVSS_II_Examples/, executes the analyzer in both report and dashboard modes with timing instrumentation wrapped around critical sections (file scan, line parsing, rule evaluation, snapshot rendering, HTML generation), and captures high-resolution timestamps using System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch. The harness should support multiple test runs to calculate average and median times, handle warm-up runs to eliminate cold-start bias, and output structured results (JSON or CSV) that can be compared against the 0.4.0 baseline. Include fixtures for the ~50MB corpus and ensure the test can run in CI or manually on developer machines.
subtasks.testStrategy: Validate the harness by running it against a small synthetic log file with known line counts, verifying that timing measurements are captured correctly and results are written to the expected output format. Confirm that the harness can successfully load and process the full ~50MB PVSS_II.log corpus without errors.

subtasks.title: Run report mode timing tests comparing against 8-minute PowerShell baseline
subtasks.description: Execute the performance harness in report mode on the ~50MB corpus, measure entire-file scan and HTML write times, and compare results against the documented 8-minute PowerShell baseline to verify the target improvement of under 5 seconds.
subtasks.details: Compare report-mode entire-file+HTML time vs ~8 min PS baseline. Record in PROGRESS. Large improvement is success; do not fail release solely for missing <5s.
subtasks.testStrategy: Execute at least 5 test runs in report mode, calculating mean and standard deviation to verify consistency. Compare the measured times against the 8-minute baseline and confirm that the speedup is documented. If results vary significantly between runs, investigate and document potential causes (disk caching, background processes).

subtasks.title: Measure dashboard cold Entire parse to inform cache decision
subtasks.description: Specifically measure the cold Entire window parse duration in dashboard mode to determine whether implementing an Entire-window cache is necessary, using the threshold of 0.5-1 second as the decision point.
subtasks.details: Extend the performance harness to launch the DesigoLogWatcher in dashboard mode, perform a cold Entire window catch-up parse on the ~50MB corpus (simulating the first dashboard load or a restart with Entire window selected), and measure the DashboardColdEntireDuration from file open through final AnalysisState snapshot generation. The test should clear any existing cache state before each run to ensure a true cold parse measurement. Run multiple iterations on both warm disk (after recent file access) and cold disk (after clearing OS file cache using tools like RAMMap or a system reboot) to understand the range of performance. Record whether the cold Entire parse exceeds the 0.5-1 second threshold specified in the PRD for cache implementation. Document the decision rationale: if cold Entire parse is under ~0.5 seconds consistently, skip the cache per PRD guidance; if it exceeds ~1 second, plan to implement the cache in subtask 8. Store all measurements with metadata (disk state, run number, duration) for inclusion in PROGRESS-V0.5.md.
subtasks.testStrategy: Execute at least 3 cold-disk runs and 3 warm-disk runs, recording minimum, maximum, and average times for each scenario. Verify that the decision threshold (0.5-1 second) is clearly documented along with the measured values. Test that cache state can be reliably cleared between runs.

subtasks.title: Run dev-gate parity tests comparing outputs against 0.4.0 with meta allowlist
subtasks.description: Perform byte-for-byte comparison of HTML, text, and JSON snapshot outputs between the new C# analyzer and 0.4.0 PowerShell version under dev-gate conditions, allowing only documented meta differences while failing on unexpected content changes.
subtasks.details: Create a parity test suite that runs both the 0.4.0 PowerShell analyzer (Watch-PvssLog.ps1 in report mode) and the new DesigoLogWatcher C# analyzer on the same static PVSS_II.log corpus, captures the HTML report, text snapshot, and JSON output from each, and performs byte-for-byte comparison using file hashing (SHA256) or text diff tools. Establish a meta differences allowlist that documents expected variations such as timestamp formats in headers, version strings (0.4.0 vs 0.5.0), generator tool names, and any other PRD-approved cosmetic changes. The test should fail with a detailed diff report if any unexpected content differences are detected (different rule counts, missing sections, altered priority classifications, changed line numbers). Store baseline outputs from 0.4.0 in a fixtures directory and implement the comparison logic as an automated test that can run in CI. The dev-gate test assumes §2.1 exceptions are not yet enabled, so rule counts and section structures should match 0.4.0 exactly at this stage.
subtasks.testStrategy: Run the parity test suite with known identical inputs and verify that only allowlisted meta differences are reported. Introduce a deliberate content change (e.g., modify a rule output) and confirm that the test correctly fails with a detailed diff. Validate that the test can run on both developer machines and CI infrastructure.

subtasks.title: Reconfirm ship-gate expectations from T8
subtasks.description: Run ship-gate suite with §2.1 enabled; ensure PROGRESS deltas match; fail unexpected diffs only.
subtasks.details: Do not re-implement §2.1 here — verify T8 + update PROGRESS if measurements reveal additional expected deltas.
subtasks.testStrategy: Execute the ship-gate parity tests with §2.1 enabled and verify that the documented deltas (rule count increases, new sections) are detected and accepted. Introduce a regression (e.g., disable an existing 0.4.0 rule) and confirm that the test correctly fails. Validate that the delta specification is comprehensive and maintainable.

subtasks.title: Validate all API contracts by comparing JSON schemas for dashboard endpoints
subtasks.description: Compare JSON response schemas for /api/pulse, /api/section, /api/manager, /api/health, and other dashboard endpoints against 0.4.0 API responses to ensure backward compatibility and contract adherence.
subtasks.details: Launch the DesigoLogWatcher dashboard mode and the 0.4.0 PowerShell dashboard (if still available) side-by-side on the same log corpus, capture JSON responses from all documented API endpoints (/api/pulse for progress and tailing status, /api/section for window snapshots, /api/manager for manager-specific data, /api/health for system status), and perform schema validation to ensure that response structures are identical or strictly backward-compatible. Use JSON schema comparison tools or custom validators to check that all required fields are present with correct types, that field names match exactly (case-sensitive), and that array structures and nesting levels are preserved. Document any intentional API enhancements (additional optional fields for §2.1 data, for example) in an API changelog and verify that clients consuming the 0.4.0 API will not break when pointed at the 0.5.0 endpoints. Create API contract tests as automated fixtures that can be run in CI, using sample log data to populate realistic responses. Include tests for edge cases (empty sections, zero progress, health check failures) to ensure robust contract coverage.
subtasks.testStrategy: Develop automated API contract tests using sample requests and expected response fixtures, asserting that JSON schemas match between 0.4.0 and 0.5.0 for all endpoints. Validate that the tests catch schema breaks by intentionally removing a required field and confirming test failure. Run the tests against both the C# dashboard and the 0.4.0 PowerShell dashboard if available.

subtasks.title: Test config behavior, launcher integration, and CLI semantics against acceptance checklist
subtasks.description: Validate configuration file loading, self-correction behavior, launcher integration (Run-Watch.cmd, Run-Report.cmd), and CLI argument semantics to ensure they match 0.4.0 workflows and acceptance criteria.
subtasks.details: Execute a comprehensive acceptance test suite covering config subsystem behavior (task 2 deliverables), launcher scripts (task 11 deliverables), and CLI semantics. Test config loading by providing valid, invalid, and edge-case watch-config.txt files and verifying that the Config class parses valid settings, self-corrects invalid ones with appropriate console warnings, and respects CLI overrides (e.g., --port, --window arguments). Test launcher integration by invoking Run-Watch.cmd and Run-Report.cmd on a clean machine and confirming that they launch DesigoLogWatcher.exe with correct arguments, that the dashboard starts on the configured port, and that report mode generates output files in expected locations. Validate CLI semantics by testing all documented arguments (log path, window selection, dashboard mode vs report mode, config file override) and ensuring they behave identically to 0.4.0 PowerShell scripts. Cross-check against the acceptance checklist documented in the PRD or task specifications, marking each criterion as pass/fail. Record any deviations or issues discovered during testing for resolution before release.
subtasks.testStrategy: Create integration tests that simulate end-user workflows: launching from cmd scripts, modifying config files, passing CLI arguments, and verifying expected behavior. Test on a machine without PowerShell installed to confirm self-contained.exe operation. Document test results against the acceptance checklist in a test report.

subtasks.title: Implement optional Entire-window cache with clone/serve/background-save
subtasks.description: If dashboard cold Entire parse exceeds the 0.5-1 second threshold (determined in subtask 3), implement an Entire-window cache that clones AnalysisState after catch-up, serves cached results on window flips, and saves cache in the background without blocking the host.
subtasks.details: If and only if T12.3 shows multi-second pain returning to Entire: implement cache with same invalidation triggers as PS; serve first, cache in background. Otherwise skip and document decision in PROGRESS.
subtasks.testStrategy: If cache is implemented, test that switching away from and back to Entire window reuses cached state without re-parsing, verify that cache invalidates correctly when new log lines are appended, and confirm that background save does not block the dashboard UI. If cache is not implemented, document the decision and verify that repeated Entire window requests still perform acceptably with measured cold parse times.

subtasks.title: Profile and optimize hotspots using instrumentation to achieve performance goals
subtasks.description: Use profiling tools (dotTrace, PerfView, Visual Studio Profiler) and existing instrumentation data to identify and optimize the top performance hotspots, targeting the aspirational goal of under 5 seconds for report mode and under 1 second stretch goal.
subtasks.details: Analyze the performance measurement data from subtasks 2 and 3 to identify the slowest components: line parsing (ReadOnlySpan usage, allocation patterns), regex matching (compiled regexes in RuleEngine), rule evaluation (per-line rule iteration, condition checks), snapshot rendering (SnapshotWriter logic), and HTML generation (template rendering, string building). Use a.NET profiler such as JetBrains dotTrace, Microsoft PerfView, or Visual Studio Profiler to capture CPU and memory profiles during a full report-mode run and dashboard cold Entire parse, focusing on methods with high inclusive time or allocation counts. Prioritize optimizations that address the top 3 hotspots by cumulative time, applying techniques such as: reducing allocations by leveraging Span<char> and ArrayPool, optimizing regex patterns or replacing them with span-based parsing where feasible, batching rule evaluations to reduce overhead, caching frequently computed values (e.g., parsed timestamps, manager names), and parallelizing independent operations if safe. After each optimization, re-run the performance tests from subtasks 2 and 3 to measure impact and ensure no regressions. Continue iterating until the aspirational target of under 5 seconds for report mode is achieved or until diminishing returns are reached. Document all optimizations, profiling findings, and performance gains in PROGRESS-V0.5.md.
subtasks.testStrategy: Capture before-and-after performance profiles for each optimization, comparing execution time and memory allocation metrics. Run the full performance test suite after optimizations to confirm improvements and detect any regressions. Validate that optimizations do not break parity tests from subtasks 4 and 5.

subtasks.title: Document all findings, decisions, and measurements in PROGRESS-V0.5.md
subtasks.description: Compile comprehensive documentation of all performance measurements, parity test results, API validation outcomes, cache implementation decisions, profiling findings, and acceptance test results into PROGRESS-V0.5.md as the final quality gate for 0.5.0 release.
subtasks.details: Create or update PROGRESS-V0.5.md with structured sections covering: (1) Performance Results – table of report mode and dashboard cold Entire parse timings, speedup ratios vs 0.4.0 baseline, hardware specs, and comparison to aspirational targets; (2) Cache Decision – cold Entire parse measurements, threshold analysis, and rationale for implementing or skipping the Entire-window cache with code references if implemented; (3) Parity Verification – dev-gate and ship-gate test results, allowlisted meta differences, documented §2.1 deltas, and any issues resolved; (4) API Contract Validation – endpoint-by-endpoint schema comparison results, backward compatibility confirmation, and changelog of any API enhancements; (5) Acceptance Testing – config behavior, launcher integration, CLI semantics test results with pass/fail status for each criterion; (6) Profiling and Optimization – hotspot analysis, optimizations applied, before-and-after performance data, and remaining known bottlenecks; (7) Outstanding Issues – any known bugs, limitations, or deferred work for future phases. Ensure the document is well-formatted with tables, code snippets, and links to relevant source files, providing a complete audit trail of the validation process. This document serves as the final sign-off artifact for stakeholders and the basis for release notes.
subtasks.testStrategy: Review PROGRESS-V0.5.md for completeness, ensuring that all subtask findings are documented with sufficient detail for reproducibility. Cross-check that all acceptance criteria from the PRD are addressed. Have a peer or stakeholder review the document to confirm it meets release documentation standards.
